00Principles

Every terminal mock on this page is drawn on a real character grid by a small ratatui-shaped engine, so widths, truncation and breakpoints behave the way the Rust code will. Switch the mock theme at the top right; NO_COLOR is the honesty test: if a state is still readable there, it is not relying on colour.

01 · attention first

Show what needs a human

Home answers "what do I do next?" before anything else. A ranked Needs you queue replaces the network chart as the dominant element.

02 · signal over decoration

Every cell earns its place

The 8-row logo and the link-speed chart leave steady state. Branding lives in one status-bar chip; network diagnostics move to the command palette.

03 · friction ∝ blast radius

Poka-yoke by default

Safe actions are one key. Reversible ones get an undo toast. Destructive ones need a hold or a typed confirm, and only when something is actually at risk.

04 · never colour alone

Glyph + label + colour

Each SessionStatus has a glyph, an ASCII fallback and a word. Colour is the third signal, never the only one.

05 · one focus signal

Thick border means "keys go here"

Exactly one panel is focused at a time: thick border plus accent title. Tab cycles focus; the footer hints change with it.

06 · degrade gracefully

Truecolor → 256 → 16 → mono

Builds on the existing ColorCapability downgrade in theme.rs and the MAESTRO_ASCII_ICONS glyph fallback.

01Audit of the v0.31.6 landing screen

MASP-style breakdown. The symptom is a slow home screen; the root cause is that it was built to show release activity, not to route the operator to the next decision.

#FindingImpactSevFix in this system

2Quit sits in the action grid as a peer of navigation, and single-key q quits. Three exit paths: q, menu Quit, ^X.Accidental exit risk when agents run; inconsistent muscle memory.HIGHQuit leaves the grid. ⌃Q everywhere; q only quits instantly when the fleet is idle, otherwise it opens hold-to-confirm.
3Release Console takes about 55% of the screen; its largest chart is internet link speed (6.77 KiB/s).Most of the screen carries no orchestration decision.HIGHLink chart moves to Network diagnostics (command palette, ⌃K → "network"). Release info shrinks to a What's new card shown for one version.

02Home: Mission Control

Same building blocks the app already has (status bar, menu, charts, release notes, activity log), recomposed around one question: what needs me? Pick a breakpoint and a state. The layout is computed, not drawn by hand.

  1. StatusBar — state only: fleet counts, budget, quota windows, trust, update, mode. Never key hints.
  2. TabBar — 1–6 jump between top-level screens; the active one is reversed. Breadcrumb lives here on deeper screens.
  3. Needs you — focused by default. Ranked: errors > agents waiting on you > ready-to-ship > quota notices. ⏎ runs the row's action.
  4. Fleet — compact view of the board: status chip, context gauge, model, cost, elapsed. f opens the full Fleet board.
  5. Actions — the old menu, grouped RUN · PLAN · INSIGHT, same letters. Quit removed. Disabled items show ⊘ and say why.
  6. Budget & quota — session spend vs cap, 5h / 7d / 7d-Sonnet windows, and which model routing picks right now.
  7. Milestone — progress, next issues, blockers. h opens Milestone Review.
  8. Insight column (wide only) — throughput Canvas, change mix, What's new. Drops out first as width shrinks.
  9. Activity — takes leftover height; level filter; / to search.
  10. Footer — hints for the focused panel only, with ⌃Q quit pinned right.

Shell rules every screen follows

Drawn from the v0.31.8 screenshots of all eight screens. Each screen section below builds on these instead of restating them.

v0.31.8 todayRuleWhy
A floating "⚠ BYPASS MODE" tab overlaps the top border on every screen.Persistent ▲ BYPASS chip in the StatusBar, reverse warn colour.A dangerous standing mode belongs in the place you read state from, not a decoration that can be clipped.

Activity Log pane fixed at the bottom of every screen (≈25% of rows), repeating the same 3–4 lines.Log lives on Home and Dashboard. Elsewhere WARN/ERR arrive as a toast; ⌃L toggles a log drawer (proposed).Gives wizards and editors the space they need; important events still interrupt.
Key hints in panel titles, under panels, and in a footer, each with a different format.Hints live only in the footer, for the focused context; ⌃Q quit pinned right.One place to look; titles stay short.

Full-screen spinners ("Loading project stats…", "Fetching milestones from GitHub…").Progressive loading: cached data or skeleton panels, with what is being fetched and from where.The screen is usable before the network answers.
Enter creates on GitHub from the preview.Armed-Enter for every external write: first ⏎ arms and states exactly what will be written, second ⏎ within 3s commits.Irreversible remote writes need a deliberate second motion.

02.1Dashboard: operations cockpit

Home answers "what needs me?". Dashboard answers "what is this piece of work doing, and what can I do to it?". The v0.31.8 Dashboard is a second launcher menu with a suggestions list; the redesign turns it into a list of running work (sessions, PR pipeline, finished) with the selected item's gates, pipeline stage, context, cost and live output beside it, and makes the restored pending PRs actionable rows instead of a log sentence.

Reimagined

  1. StatusBar · TabBar — tab 2 Dashboard active. Fleet counts, budget, quota and ▲ BYPASS stay in the status bar, so the body never repeats them.
  2. View strip — o Ops (default) · c Cost · t Tokens · g Deps. F4 F5 F6 still work. Right side: one summary line.
  3. Work — focused by default. Three groups, one selection: Sessions (pool), PR pipeline (open PRs under CI polling and restored PendingPrs), Finished · this run. Overflow shows ↓ n more on the border.
  4. Session detail — status, model, elapsed, cost, retries; issue title; branch and worktree; Pipeline stepper run ─ gates ─ push ─ PR ─ CI; Gates from gate_results; Context · cost; Output tail, newest at the bottom.
  5. PR detail — status and attempt counters, last errors (up to 3, as kept by last_errors), and the exact gh pr create it will run. ⏎ arms, ⏎ again within 3s writes.
  6. Activity — full width at the bottom, because the log lives on Home and Dashboard only. Messages are not cut mid-word.
  7. Footer — hints for the selected row type: a failed-gates session offers r re-run gates and v gate output; a PR row offers the armed ⏎.

Why Dashboard is not a second Home

Home already owns the ranked Needs you queue and a compact fleet table. Dashboard must not compete with it, so the three "status" screens split by depth, not by data:

ScreenQuestionUnitTypical action
Home (tab 1)What needs me, across everything?One line per attention item⏎ jumps to the item; for sessions and PRs that means Dashboard with the row selected.
Dashboard (tab 2)What is this work doing, and what can I do to it?One session or PR, in depthRetry gates, open output, create a pending PR, pause, kill.
Fleet board (f on Home)What Claude Code work exists on this machine?Pool + external + adopted transcriptsAdopt, open, inspect. Read-mostly.
  • Dashboard absorbs Overview. TuiMode::Overview (the panel grid) and TuiMode::Dashboard (the launcher) merge into one mode. The grid's per-panel cards become the work list plus one detail pane, which reads better at every width than N squeezed panels.
  • The Quick Actions list is deleted, not moved. Navigation lives in the TabBar, Home's Actions and the ⌃K palette. A launcher on tab 2 is the same thing as Home with worse letters.
  • No attention queue here. Dashboard sorts its own rows by group, then status urgency, but it never shows quota or milestone rows; those are Home's.
  • Cost, Tokens and Deps are sub-views of Dashboard, not separate tabs, because they are about the same running work. TurboQuant savings is a cost and token metric, so it becomes a card in Cost and a section of Tokens instead of a fourth key (Q).

// src/tui/screens/dashboard/rows.rs (proposed)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum WorkKey { Session(uuid::Uuid), PendingPr(u64), OpenPr(u64), Header(Group) }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum Group { Sessions, PrPipeline, Finished }

pub struct WorkList { pub rows: Vec<WorkKey>, pub selected: Option<WorkKey> }

impl WorkList {
    pub fn rebuild(&mut self, app: &App) {
        let mut rows = vec![WorkKey::Header(Group::Sessions)];
        // FailedGates is terminal but still actionable (re-run gates), so it stays in Sessions.
        let done = |s: &&Session| matches!(s.status, SessionStatus::Completed | SessionStatus::Killed);
        rows.extend(app.pool.all_sessions().iter()
            .filter(|s| !done(s))
            .map(|s| WorkKey::Session(s.id)));
        rows.push(WorkKey::Header(Group::PrPipeline));
        rows.extend(app.ci_poller.ci_check_details.keys().map(|pr| WorkKey::OpenPr(*pr)));
        rows.extend(app.pending_prs.iter().map(|p| WorkKey::PendingPr(p.issue_number)));
        rows.push(WorkKey::Header(Group::Finished));
        rows.extend(app.pool.all_sessions().iter()
            .filter(done)
            .map(|s| WorkKey::Session(s.id)));
        // Selection survives reordering: keep the key, fall back to the first row.
        if !self.selected.is_some_and(|k| rows.contains(&k)) {
            self.selected = rows.iter().copied().find(|k| !matches!(k, WorkKey::Header(_)));
        }
        self.rows = rows;
    }
}

/// (current step, failed step) for the run ─ gates ─ push ─ PR ─ CI stepper.
pub fn pipeline_stage(s: &Session) -> (usize, Option<usize>) {
    use SessionStatus::*;
    match s.status {
        Queued | Spawning | Running | Retrying | Stalled | Paused | NeedsReview | Interactive => (0, None),
        GatesRunning => (1, None),
        FailedGates => (1, Some(1)),
        NeedsPr => (3, None),
        CiFix | ConflictFix => (4, Some(4)),
        Completed => (5, None),
        Errored | Killed => (0, Some(0)),
    }
}


// Armed-Enter for external writes (shared with the wizards' final step).
const ARM_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

pub struct Armed { key: WorkKey, at: Instant }

pub enum EnterOutcome { Armed, Commit(WorkKey), Locked(&'static str) }

impl DashboardScreen {
    fn on_enter(&mut self, app: &App, now: Instant) -> EnterOutcome {
        let Some(key @ WorkKey::PendingPr(issue)) = self.list.selected else { return EnterOutcome::Armed };
        if !app.gh_auth_ok { return EnterOutcome::Locked("gh auth expired"); }
        let pending = app.pending_prs.iter().find(|p| p.issue_number == issue);
        if pending.is_some_and(|p| p.status == PendingPrStatus::PermanentlyFailed) {
            return EnterOutcome::Locked("retries stopped");
        }
        match self.armed.take() {
            Some(a) if a.key == key && now.duration_since(a.at) <= ARM_WINDOW => EnterOutcome::Commit(key),
            _ => { self.armed = Some(Armed { key, at: now }); EnterOutcome::Armed }
        }
    }
}
// Commit(WorkKey::PendingPr(n)) => app.trigger_manual_pr_retry(n). Any other key clears `armed`;

Implementation


    

  • Steps (types.rs): keep the enum for state, but drive the stepper from a new IssueWizardStep::STEPPER = [BasicInfo, DorFields, Dependencies, AiReview, Preview]. Remove Context; fold TypeSelect into BasicInfo as a Focus::Type stop. Creating, Complete and Failed stay as states and render inside the create gate on Preview (proposed).
    • 

  • Validation (mod.rs): validation_error() -> Option<&'static str> becomes validation_errors() -> Vec<(FieldId, Cow<str>)>, which feeds field borders, the checklist and try_advance (focus the first one). Add ExpectedBehavior. Keep a touched: BTreeSet<FieldId> so untouched empty fields show only in the checklist, not in red (proposed).
    • 

  • Focus styling: refresh_field_blocks switches from border_focused plus DIM to ds::panel with Focus::Active (thick, accent_info for text input) and plain Focus::Inactive, no DIM.
    • 

  • Frame (widgets/wizard_frame.rs): the 3-row header becomes a 1-row ds::stepper; the footer error line goes away; on Breakpoint::Wide the body splits [Fill(1), Length(42)] for the checklist. This is shared with the milestone wizard.
    • 

  • Blocked by: add dep_filter: String and dep_visible() -> Vec<usize> (substring match on #number, title and labels). dep_selected indexes the visible list; chips come from dep_checked.
    • 

  • AI improve (draw_diff.rs, mod.rs): add decisions: [Decision; 8] (Pending | Accepted | KeptMine) aligned with diff_fields(). Accept merges per field, so the trusted-seat re-stamping in parse_improve_response is unchanged. Add one line to build_improve_prompt: "If a fact is unknown, keep the user's text instead of writing a placeholder". It helps, but the lint is still the control.
    • 

  • Markdown: a small ds::markdown::lines(&str, &Theme) -> Vec<Line> for headings, bullets, **bold**, `code` and TODO chips, used by the critique, the diff and Preview. No new dependency.
    • 

  • Draft (proposed): #[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)] on IssueCreationPayload, written to .maestro/drafts/issue.json on each step change and every 10 s while dirty, restored by IssueWizardScreen::new, deleted on IssueCreated(Ok).
    • 



// issue_wizard/lint.rs (proposed): the gate's single source of truth
pub struct Placeholder { pub field: FieldId, pub line: usize }

pub fn placeholders(p: &IssueCreationPayload) -> Vec<Placeholder> {
    FieldId::ALL.iter().flat_map(|&field| {
        field.payload_ref(p).lines().enumerate()
            .filter(|(_, l)| l.contains("[TODO:"))
            .map(move |(line, _)| Placeholder { field, line })
    }).collect()
}

// Inline TODO chip for Preview and the diff: reversed warn, so it survives NO_COLOR.
pub fn todo_spans<'a>(line: &'a str, t: &Theme) -> Vec<Span<'a>> {
    let Some(start) = line.find("[TODO:") else { return vec![Span::raw(line)] };
    let end = line[start..].find(']').map_or(line.len(), |e| start + e + 1);
    vec![
        Span::raw(&line[..start]),
        Span::styled(" TODO ", Style::new().fg(t.accent_warning).add_modifier(Modifier::REVERSED | Modifier::BOLD)),
        Span::styled(line[start + 6..end - 1].trim_start(), Style::new().fg(t.accent_warning)),
        Span::raw(&line[end..]),
    ]
}


// mod.rs: Preview input. begin_create() stays the only path to TuiCommand::CreateIssue.
const ARM_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

IssueWizardStep::Preview => match code {
    KeyCode::Enter => {
        let now = self.clock.now(); // injectable for tests
        if let Some(first) = lint::placeholders(&self.payload).first() {
            self.create_armed_at = None;
            self.jump_to_field(first.field, first.line);   // Basics or Details, cursor on the line
        } else if self.create_armed_at.is_some_and(|t| now.duration_since(t) <= ARM_WINDOW) {
            self.create_armed_at = None;
            self.begin_create();
        } else {
            self.create_armed_at = Some(now);               // gate: "⏎ again to create · 3s"
        }
    }
    KeyCode::Esc if self.create_armed_at.is_some() => self.create_armed_at = None,
    KeyCode::Esc => { self.retreat(); }
    KeyCode::Char('n') => self.focus_next_placeholder(),
    KeyCode::Char('l') => self.ready_label = !self.ready_label, // render_labels(p, self.ready_label)
    _ => {}
},

// milestone_wizard/mod.rs — selected issues that level_buckets() would silently skip.
pub fn stranded(issues: &[AiProposedIssue]) -> Vec<(usize, Vec<usize>)> {
    issues
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, it)| it.accepted)
        .filter_map(|(i, it)| {
            let missing: Vec<usize> = it
                .blocked_by
                .iter()
                .copied()
                .filter(|&d| issues.get(d).is_none_or(|dep| !dep.accepted))
                .collect();
            (!missing.is_empty()).then_some((i, missing))
        })
        .collect()
}

// Property test: after stranded() is empty, every accepted issue gets a level.
#[test]
fn no_accepted_issue_is_dropped_when_nothing_is_stranded() {
    let plan = fixtures::plan_with_chain(); // P1 ← P5 ← P7, P4 ← P6
    assert!(stranded(&plan.issues).is_empty());
    let placed: usize = level_buckets(&plan.issues).iter().map(Vec::len).sum();
    assert_eq!(placed, plan.issues.iter().filter(|i| i.accepted).count());
}


// ds/armed_enter.rs — shared by the issue and milestone wizards.
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
pub const ARM_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

#[derive(Default)]
pub struct ArmedEnter { armed_at: Option<Instant> }

pub enum Armed { Armed, Commit, Disarmed }

impl ArmedEnter {
    pub fn on_enter(&mut self, now: Instant) -> Armed {
        match self.armed_at.take() {
            Some(t) if now.duration_since(t) <= ARM_WINDOW => Armed::Commit,
            _ => { self.armed_at = Some(now); Armed::Armed }
        }
    }
    /// Any other key, or the tick after the window, disarms.
    pub fn disarm(&mut self) { self.armed_at = None; }
    pub fn remaining(&self, now: Instant) -> Option<Duration> {
        self.armed_at.map(|t| ARM_WINDOW.saturating_sub(now.duration_since(t)))
    }
}

// draw: the count and the repo are part of the button label.
fn armed_line(n_issues: usize, repo: &str, t: &Theme) -> Line<'static> {
    Line::from(vec![
        Span::styled(" ⏎ ", Style::new().fg(t.accent_warning).add_modifier(Modifier::REVERSED | Modifier::BOLD)),
        Span::raw(" again to create "),
        Span::styled(format!("1 milestone + {n_issues} issues"), Style::new().add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
        Span::raw(" on "),
        Span::styled(repo.to_string(), Style::new().fg(t.accent_identifier).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
    ])
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub enum Section<T> { #[default] Loading, Ready(T), Failed(String) }

pub enum StatsPart {
    Local(SessionMetrics),                       // state.json + pool: instant
    Milestones(anyhow::Result<Vec<MilestoneProgress>>),
    Issues(anyhow::Result<IssueTrend>),
}

impl ProjectStatsScreen {
    pub fn set_part(&mut self, part: StatsPart) {
        let fail = |e: anyhow::Error| Section::Failed(format!("{e:#}"));
        match part {
            StatsPart::Local(m) => self.sessions = Section::Ready(m),
            StatsPart::Milestones(r) => self.milestones = r.map_or_else(fail, Section::Ready),
            StatsPart::Issues(r) => self.issues = r.map_or_else(fail, Section::Ready),
        }
    }
}

pub fn risk(m: &MilestoneProgress, today: NaiveDate, running: &Version) -> Risk {
    if m.semver().is_some_and(|v| v < *running) { return Risk::Stale; }
    let Some(due) = m.due_on else { return Risk::NoDue };
    let weeks_left = ((due - today).num_days().max(1) as f64) / 7.0;
    let needed = m.open() as f64 / weeks_left;
    if m.open() == 0 || m.closed_per_week >= needed { Risk::OnTrack } else { Risk::AtRisk { needed } }
}


use ratatui::{Frame, layout::Rect, symbols::Marker,
    widgets::canvas::{Canvas, Line, Points}};

fn render_trend(f: &mut Frame, area: Rect, t: &IssueTrend, theme: &Theme, lo: f64, hi: f64) {
    let n = t.weeks.len() as f64 - 1.0;
    let chart = Canvas::default()
        .marker(Marker::Braille)
        .x_bounds([0.0, n])
        .y_bounds([lo, hi])                           // one shared scale for both series
        .paint(move |ctx| {
            for (i, w) in t.weeks.windows(2).enumerate() {
                ctx.draw(&Line::new(i as f64, w[0].closed as f64,
                    (i + 1) as f64, w[1].closed as f64, theme.accent_success));
            }
            let opened: Vec<(f64, f64)> = t.weeks.iter().enumerate()
                .map(|(i, w)| (i as f64, w.opened as f64)).collect();
            ctx.draw(&Points { coords: &opened, color: theme.text_muted }); // dotted = readable in NO_COLOR
        });
    f.render_widget(chart, area);
}

// state.rs (proposed) — health drives the glyph, the doc strip count and Next steps
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SectionHealth { Complete, Thin, Empty }

impl PrdSection {
    pub fn health(self, prd: &Prd, now: DateTime<Utc>) -> SectionHealth {
        use SectionHealth::*;
        match self {
            Self::Vision => match prd.vision.trim().chars().count() {
                0 => Empty, 1..=79 => Thin, _ => Complete,
            },
            Self::Goals => match prd.goals.len() { 0 => Empty, 1 | 2 => Thin, _ => Complete },
            Self::NonGoals => if prd.non_goals.is_empty() { Empty } else { Complete },
            Self::Stakeholders => if prd.stakeholders.is_empty() { Empty } else { Complete },
            Self::CurrentState => match prd.synced_at {
                None => Empty,
                Some(t) if now - t > chrono::Duration::hours(24) => Thin,
                Some(_) => Complete,
            },
            Self::Timeline => match prd.timeline.as_slice() {
                [] => Empty,
                tl if tl.iter().all(|m| m.target_date.is_none()) => Thin,
                _ => Complete,
            },
        }
    }
}


// draw.rs — two-line section rows; glyph + word carry state without colour
fn section_item<'a>(s: PrdSection, prd: &Prd, sel: bool, t: &Theme) -> ListItem<'a> {
    let (glyph, style) = match s.health(prd, Utc::now()) {
        SectionHealth::Complete => ("✓", Style::new().fg(t.accent_success)),
        SectionHealth::Thin => ("!", Style::new().fg(t.accent_warning).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
        SectionHealth::Empty => ("○", Style::new().fg(t.text_muted)),
    };
    let marker = if sel { "▌" } else { " " };
    ListItem::new(vec![
        Line::from(vec![Span::raw(marker), Span::styled(glyph, style), Span::raw(" "),
                        Span::styled(s.label(), Style::new().add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD))]),
        Line::from(vec![Span::raw("   "), Span::styled(summary(s, prd), Style::new().fg(t.text_muted))]),
    ])
}

// List::highlight_style(selection) + ds::panel("Sections", focus, t) handle the rest.

/// Schedule health: glyph + word + colour. Never colour alone.
pub enum Health { Late(u32), AtRisk, OnTrack, NoDate, Done }

impl Health {
    pub fn of(m: &Milestone, today: NaiveDate) -> Self {
        let total = m.open_issues + m.closed_issues;
        if total > 0 && m.open_issues == 0 { return Self::Done; }
        let Some(due) = m.due_on.as_deref().and_then(parse_ymd) else { return Self::NoDate };
        let days = (due - today).num_days();
        let done = f64::from(m.closed_issues) / f64::from(total.max(1));
        match days {
            d if d < 0 => Self::Late(d.unsigned_abs() as u32),
            d if d <= 7 && done < 0.8 => Self::AtRisk,
            _ => Self::OnTrack,
        }
    }
    pub fn span(&self, t: &Theme) -> Span<'static> {
        let (g, word, style) = match self {
            Self::Late(d) => ("✗", format!("late {d}d"), Style::new().fg(t.accent_error).bold()),
            Self::AtRisk  => ("◐", "at risk".into(),  Style::new().fg(t.accent_warning).bold()),
            Self::OnTrack => ("●", "on track".into(), Style::new().fg(t.accent_success)),
            Self::NoDate  => ("·", "no date".into(),  Style::new().fg(t.text_muted)),
            Self::Done    => ("✓", "done".into(),     Style::new().fg(t.status_completed)),
        };
        Span::styled(format!("{g} {word}"), style) // g via icons:: for ASCII fallback
    }
}


/// Longest blocked-by chain among open issues (proposed, next to dep_levels).
/// Levels are computed on the UNFILTERED set; filters only hide rows.
pub fn critical_path(inputs: &[(u64, Vec<u64>)]) -> Result<Vec<u64>, DepLevelError> {
    let levels = dep_levels(inputs)?;
    let blockers: HashMap<u64, &Vec<u64>> = inputs.iter().map(|(n, b)| (*n, b)).collect();
    let mut best: HashMap<u64, (usize, Option<u64>)> = HashMap::new();
    for level in &levels {
        for &n in level {
            let prev = blockers[&n].iter()
                .filter_map(|b| best.get(b).map(|(d, _)| (*d, *b)))
                .max();
            best.insert(n, prev.map_or((1, None), |(d, b)| (d + 1, Some(b))));
        }
    }
    let Some((&tail, _)) = best.iter().max_by_key(|(_, (d, _))| *d) else { return Ok(vec![]) };
    let (mut cur, mut path) = (tail, vec![tail]);
    while let Some(&(_, Some(p))) = best.get(&cur) { path.push(p); cur = p; }
    path.reverse();
    Ok(path)
}

02.7Milestone review


Milestone review checks one milestone against the Definition of Ready and its dependency graph, then proposes a corrected milestone description and writes it to GitHub. The redesign turns the picker into a health overview, groups findings by severity with a fix for each, and replaces three reflexive Enters with per-change selection plus one armed write that states its count.


What the code actually does (src/milestone_health/, src/tui/screens/milestone_health/): one gh issue list --milestone … --state open --limit 100 call, then deterministic local checks (check_issues, analyze). There is no AI call and no cost. The only write is patch_milestone_description: one PATCH that replaces the milestone description with generate_patch() output. Issue bodies are never edited, so Definition-of-Ready failures can only be reported, not fixed, by this screen.

// milestone_health/severity.rs (proposed): one place that ranks findings.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum Severity { Blocker, Warning, Notice }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Fix { Patch, PatchLists, EditIssue, Manual }

pub fn classify_anomaly(a: &GraphAnomaly) -> (Severity, Fix) {
    use GraphAnomaly::*;
    match a {
        CircularDependency { .. } => (Severity::Blocker, Fix::PatchLists),
        MissingDependencyGraphSection => (Severity::Blocker, Fix::Patch),
        WrongLevelAssignment { .. } | IssueMissingFromGraph { .. } => (Severity::Warning, Fix::Patch),
        CrossMilestoneBlockedBy { .. } => (Severity::Warning, Fix::Manual),
        MissingSequenceLine | GraphReferencesUnknownIssue { .. } => (Severity::Notice, Fix::Patch),
    }
}

pub fn classify_missing(m: &MissingField) -> (Severity, Fix) {
    match m {
        MissingField::Section(_) => (Severity::Warning, Fix::EditIssue),
        MissingField::WeakAcceptanceCriteria | MissingField::WeakBlockedBy => (Severity::Notice, Fix::EditIssue),
    }
}

pub fn glyph(s: Severity) -> (&'static str, &'static str) {
    match s { Severity::Blocker => ("✗", "blocker"), Severity::Warning => ("!", "warning"), Severity::Notice => ("○", "notice") }
}


// state.rs (proposed): armed-Enter on the Changes step. Pure reducer; `now` is injected for tests.
const ARM_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

(HealthInput::Key(KeyCode::Enter, now), HealthStep::Changes { milestone, changes, armed, .. }) => {
    let accepted: Vec<bool> = changes.iter().map(|c| c.accepted).collect();
    match *armed {
        Some(t) if now.duration_since(t) <= ARM_WINDOW => {
            let description = generate_patch_with(milestone, &self.issues, &self.anomalies(), &accepted);
            let milestone = milestone.clone();
            self.step = HealthStep::Writing { milestone: milestone.clone(), last_proposed: description.clone() };
            HealthSideEffect::DispatchPatch { milestone_number: milestone.number, description }
        }
        _ => { *armed = Some(now); HealthSideEffect::None } // first ⏎, or the window expired: (re)arm
    }
}
(HealthInput::Key(_, _), HealthStep::Changes { armed: armed @ Some(_), .. }) => {
    *armed = None; // any other key disarms, and does nothing else
    HealthSideEffect::None
}

// src/tui/widgets/launch_dialog.rs (proposed). pool.session_for_issue and state.total_cost_usd are
// placeholder names for the existing pool lookup and the run's cost total.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum LaunchMode { #[default] Autonomous, ChatUntilPr, ChatOpen }

impl LaunchMode {
    /// (produce_pr, interaction), the flags SessionConfig already carries.
    pub fn flags(self) -> (bool, bool) {
        match self {
            LaunchMode::Autonomous => (true, false),
            LaunchMode::ChatUntilPr => (true, true),
            LaunchMode::ChatOpen => (false, true),
        }
    }
    /// [behavior.launch] defaults keep working: (_, false) is Autonomous.
    pub fn from_defaults((produce_pr, interaction): (bool, bool)) -> Self {
        match (interaction, produce_pr) {
            (false, _) => LaunchMode::Autonomous,
            (true, true) => LaunchMode::ChatUntilPr,
            (true, false) => LaunchMode::ChatOpen,
        }
    }
}

pub enum LaunchBlock { Claimed { issue: u64, session: uuid::Uuid }, BudgetCap { worst: f64, left: f64 } }

pub fn launch_block(app: &App, issues: &[u64], sessions: usize) -> Option<LaunchBlock> {
    if let Some((issue, s)) = issues.iter().find_map(|n| app.pool.session_for_issue(*n).map(|s| (*n, s.id))) {
        return Some(LaunchBlock::Claimed { issue, session: s });
    }
    let b = &app.config.as_ref()?.budget;
    let worst = sessions as f64 * b.per_session_usd;
    let left = b.total_usd - app.state.total_cost_usd;
    (worst > left).then_some(LaunchBlock::BudgetCap { worst, left })
}


// list.rs (proposed): one glyph per row, most urgent first. Never colour alone.
pub enum RowState { AgentHere(SessionStatus), Blocked(u64), ClaimedElsewhere, PrOpen(u64), Free }

pub fn row_state(issue: &Issue, app: &App, open: &HashSet<u64>) -> RowState {
    if let Some(s) = app.pool.session_for_issue(issue.number) { return RowState::AgentHere(s.status); }
    if let Some(b) = issue.all_blockers().into_iter().find(|b| open.contains(b)) { return RowState::Blocked(b); }
    if issue.labels.iter().any(|l| l == MaestroLabel::InProgress.as_str()) { return RowState::ClaimedElsewhere; }
    if let Some(p) = app.pending_prs.iter().find(|p| p.issue_number == issue.number) { return RowState::PrOpen(p.issue_number); }
    RowState::Free
}

fn row_line(row: &IssueRow, cols: &Cols, cursor: bool, list_focused: bool, theme: &Theme) -> Line<'static> {
    let (glyph, style) = row.state.glyph(theme);              // ● ⊘ ◇ ⇡ ○
    let ready = if row.dor.passed() { Span::styled("✓ 7/7", theme.ok()) }
                else { Span::styled(format!("! {}/7", row.dor_ok), theme.warn()) };
    let mut spans = vec![
        Span::raw(if cursor && list_focused { "▌" } else if cursor { "›" } else { " " }),
        Span::raw(if row.selected { "✓ " } else { "  " }),
        Span::styled(format!("#{:<5}", row.number), theme.identifier()),
        Span::styled(format!("{glyph} "), style),
        Span::raw(truncate_ellipsis(&row.title, cols.title)),
    ];
    if cols.labels > 0 { spans.push(Span::styled(pad(&row.labels, cols.labels), theme.label())); }
    spans.extend([Span::raw(pad(&row.milestone_short, cols.ms)), ready]);
    let line = Line::from(spans);
    if cursor && list_focused { line.style(focused_selection_style(theme)) } else { line }
}

// src/work/run_plan.rs (proposed): one pure function feeds the START column, the issue
// levels, the preview card and the Run queue screen, and it is the thing the tests pin.
use crate::orchestration::dag::{classify_edges, topo_levels, Edge, IssueMeta};
use crate::work::conflicts::{predict_conflicts, IssueWithFiles};
use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};

pub enum Hold { StaleClaim, BlockedOutside { by: u64, milestone: Option<u64> }, WaitsOnDeferred(u64) }

pub struct RunPlan {
    pub waves: Vec<Vec<u64>>,          // launch order; wave n+1 starts as wave n frees slots
    pub decide: Vec<(u64, Hold)>,       // ⏎ is locked while this is non-empty
    pub deferred: Vec<(u64, Hold)>,
    pub moved: Vec<(u64, u64, String)>, // (issue, after, shared file): "⇄ after #969"
    pub unknown_scope: Vec<u64>,
}

pub fn plan_run(
    open: &HashSet<u64>, milestone: u64, metas: &HashMap<u64, IssueMeta>,
    claimed: &HashSet<u64>, files: &HashMap<u64, Option<Vec<String>>>,
) -> anyhow::Result<RunPlan> {
    let edges = classify_edges(open, Some(milestone), metas);
    let mut held: HashMap<u64, Hold> = HashMap::new();
    for (&n, es) in &edges {
        if let Some(Edge::CrossMilestoneOpenExternal(by)) = es.iter().find(|e| matches!(e, Edge::CrossMilestoneOpenExternal(_))) {
            held.insert(n, Hold::BlockedOutside { by: *by, milestone: metas.get(by).and_then(|m| m.milestone) });
        }
    }
    claimed.iter().filter(|n| open.contains(n)).for_each(|&n| { held.entry(n).or_insert(Hold::StaleClaim); });
    // propagate: anything that waits (in-slice) on a held issue is deferred too, to a fixed point
    loop {
        let before = held.len();
        for (&n, es) in &edges {
            if held.contains_key(&n) { continue; }
            if let Some(Edge::InSlice(dep)) = es.iter().find(|e| matches!(e, Edge::InSlice(d) if held.contains_key(d))) {
                held.insert(n, Hold::WaitsOnDeferred(*dep));
            }
        }
        if held.len() == before { break; }
    }
    let runnable: HashSet<u64> = open.iter().copied().filter(|n| !held.contains_key(n)).collect();
    let mut waves = topo_levels(&runnable, &edges)?;
    let moved = split_same_wave_overlaps(&mut waves, files); // later issue → next wave, via predict_conflicts
    let unknown_scope = runnable.iter().copied().filter(|n| matches!(files.get(n), None | Some(None))).collect();
    let (decide, deferred) = held.into_iter().partition(|(_, h)| matches!(h, Hold::StaleClaim));
    Ok(RunPlan { waves, decide, deferred, moved, unknown_scope })
}



// Milestone row: one Line, progress in one colour, START never dropped (ratatui 0.29).
fn milestone_row(e: &MilestoneEntry, ready: usize, w: u16, sel: bool, t: &Theme) -> Line<'static> {
    let show_bar = w >= 56;
    let name_w = w as usize - 1 - 7 - 5 - 2 - if show_bar { 9 } else { 0 };
    let mut spans = vec![
        Span::raw(if sel { "▌" } else { " " }),
        Span::styled(truncate(&e.title, name_w), Style::new().fg(t.text_primary)),
        Span::raw(" "),
    ];
    if show_bar {
        let filled = (e.progress_ratio() * 8.0).round() as usize;
        spans.push(Span::styled("█".repeat(filled), Style::new().fg(t.accent_info)));
        spans.push(Span::styled("░".repeat(8 - filled), Style::new().fg(t.text_muted).add_modifier(Modifier::DIM)));
        spans.push(Span::raw(" "));
    }
    spans.push(Span::raw(format!("{:>5} ", format!("{}/{}", e.closed_issues, e.total_issues()))));
    spans.push(match (e.open_issues, ready) {
        (0, _) => Span::styled(" ✓ done", Style::new().fg(t.status_completed)),
        (_, 0) => Span::styled("0 ready", Style::new().fg(t.text_muted)),
        (_, n) => Span::styled(format!("{n:>1} ready"), Style::new().fg(t.accent_success)),
    });
    let line = Line::from(spans);
    if sel { line.style(focused_selection_style(t)) } else { line }
}

The redesign makes ⏎ a newline, puts the run settings in a strip under the composer, and routes ⌃S through the same launch dialog that Issues uses.

  3. Recent prompts (empty composer only): the last six entries with outcome glyph, age and line count. The panel title says ↑ opens history. As soon as you type, the composer takes the space.
    4. 
  
  4. Run settings: always visible, and exactly what ⌃S will launch. Issue (link or mention), Mode (the launchDialog radio, with a consequence line in words), Agent (agent, model, session mode), Where (worktree and branch from session_slug()), Cost (projector floor, per-session cap, what is left).
    5. 
  
  5. Context (Wide only): linked issues resolved from the issue cache, attachments, and a numbered Sent to the agent list (issue prompt, your text, image paths, mode instructions, bypass). On Regular and Compact this becomes a one-line strip under the composer.
    6. 
  
  6. Launch dialog (⌃S): issue_browser's launchDialog, prompt flavour. The prompt is read-only there; Esc goes back to edit it. ⏎ launches. It writes nothing to GitHub, so there is no armed second press, as SYNC requires.
    7. 
  
  7. Footer: hints for the focused context only. ⌃S review & run comes first; ⏎ newline is listed so the change is discoverable.
    8. 



Why ⌃S and not ⏎. In a multi-line editor ⏎ is the most-pressed key, so it must be the safe one. Spawning needs a chord that every terminal delivers. ⇧⏎ and ⌃⏎ don't qualify: without PushKeyboardEnhancementFlags they arrive as ⏎. ⌃J is delivered (LF in raw mode becomes Char('j') + CONTROL) but it is today's newline, and swapping meanings would punish existing muscle memory. ⌃S is delivered because crossterm's raw mode clears IXON, it has no tui-textarea binding, and "save / send" is a common reading of it. It still only opens a dialog. Where supports_keyboard_enhancement() is true, ⌃⏎ is also accepted (proposed). A user who presses ⏎ twice expecting the old submit gets a blank line, which costs nothing.

Implementation


    

  • Input (prompt_input/mod.rs): in the editor arm, (KeyCode::Enter, _) always calls insert_newline(). A new (KeyCode::Char('s'), CONTROL) arm returns ScreenAction::OpenLaunchDialog (proposed) when the trimmed text isn't empty. ⌃U is removed and ⌃Z calls self.editor.undo(). ↑ opens History only if editor_text().is_empty().
    • 

  • State (types.rs): produce_pr, interaction and unified_pr become mode: LaunchMode (shared with issue_browser) and link: IssueLink { None, Issue(u64), Unified(Vec<u64>) }. FocusRing becomes [EDITOR, SETTINGS, ATTACHMENTS], and ATTACHMENTS is skipped while image_paths is empty. status_message is replaced by a toast.
    • 

  • Launch (tui/mod.rs LaunchPromptSession): build the session with .with_image_paths(paths) and drop the [Attached image: …] text. Pass produce_pr and interaction through. IssueLink::Issue(n) sends ScreenAction::LaunchSession(SessionConfig { issue_number: Some(n), custom_prompt: Some(text), .. }), which already exists. Wire DefaultBudgetProjector::new(per_session_usd, 0.10) where budget_enforcer is built (screen_dispatch.rs:1053), so the pre-spawn gate and the displayed estimate use the same numbers.
    • 

  • Images: the add-path and paste paths call session::image::validate_image_path. The error is shown on the field border.
    • 

  • Draft (proposed): the Pop arm moves editor_text() and image_paths into app.prompt_draft instead of dropping them. create_prompt_input_screen restores them.
    • 

  • Refs: refresh_detected_refs also looks each number up in the issue cache used for autocomplete. The strip and the dialog read (number, Option<title>); Unified keeps only resolved numbers.
    • 



// prompt_input/mod.rs: editor arm (proposed). ⏎ can no longer spawn.
if self.is_prompt_editor_focused() {
    match (code, *modifiers) {
        (KeyCode::Char('s'), KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
            return if self.editor_text().trim().is_empty() {
                self.toast = Some(Toast::warn("Nothing to run · type a prompt first"));
                ScreenAction::None
            } else {
                ScreenAction::OpenLaunchDialog(self.launch_request())   // same dialog as Issues
            };
        }
        (KeyCode::Enter, _) | (KeyCode::Char('j'), KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => self.editor.insert_newline(),
        (KeyCode::Char('z'), KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => { self.editor.undo(); }
        (KeyCode::Up, _) if self.editor_text().is_empty() && !self.history.is_empty() => {
            self.history_view = Some(HistoryView::new(self.history.len() - 1));
        }
        _ => { self.editor.input(event.clone()); self.refresh_detected_refs(); }
    }
}


// tui/mod.rs: LaunchPromptSession (proposed). Images are attached for real; options are honoured.
let paths: Vec<PathBuf> = config.image_paths.iter().map(PathBuf::from).collect();
let session = Session::new(config.prompt.clone(), model, mode, None, None)
    .with_mode_config(mode_config)
    .with_agent_id(Some(agent_id))
    .with_image_paths(paths)                // pool.rs copies them into the worktree
    .with_launch(config.produce_pr, config.interaction); // (proposed) same fields as SessionConfig
if config.interaction {
    open_prompt_interaction_session(app, session);   // (proposed) twin of open_interaction_session
} else {
    app.pending_session_launches.push(session);
}

02.11Adapt project


Adapt reads a project, asks Claude what it is made of, and turns that into a PRD, .claude/ files, and milestones and issues on GitHub. The core change: the five bare form rows become a run you can predict. Each option states what it reads, sends and writes. The pipeline pauses for review before any write. The result tells "created", "nothing to do", "looks wrong" and "failed" apart.



Audit of v0.31.8

StopAfterPicker. It replaces Dry Run / Scan Only / No Issues and maps onto the same AdaptConfig booleans, so the pipeline code doesn't change. Each option says what it adds and whether it writes. The model picker uses the segmented style of the issue wizard's type toggle.

OutcomeHeader: four outcomes that v0.31.8 drew with one success banner. "Up to date" is a real plan where every item already exists, shown with the existing numbers. "Looks wrong" is a phase that returned less than the project can explain. "Failed" is a phase error, with what was already written.

Implementation


    

  • Stop after. Add StopAfter { Scan, Analysis, Plan, Full } to adapt/types.rs (screen) with apply(&self, cfg: &mut AdaptWizardConfig). It sets the existing scan_only / no_issues / dry_run, so complete_* and the CLI flags stay as they are. Make Plan the default.
    • 

  • Review pause. Add AdaptStep::Review. When dry_run is false, complete_plan() now sets Review and returns None instead of RunAdaptScaffold. The second ⏎ inside the armed window returns ScreenAction::StartAdaptPipeline with step = Scaffolding, and dispatch already handles that branch. armed_at: Option<Instant> works as in the wizards (ds::ArmedEnter).
    • 

  • Cache. Store a CacheKey { root, model, stop_after, written_at } next to the results, and move the file to <project>/.maestro/adapt-cache.json (path-relative, not CWD-relative). cache_path() takes the root, and tests pass a tempdir.
    • 

  • PRD write. Remove the write from RunAdaptConsolidate. Write in a new RunAdaptWrite before scaffold, using write_no_follow, and record it in a WrittenFile list next to ScaffoldResult.files.
    • 

  • Progress and cancel. Stamp phase_started: Instant on every transition, and fill a PhaseRecord { step, elapsed, model, summary } list. Pass a tokio_util::sync::CancellationToken to the spawned tasks and select! it against run_text. Check it between items in RepoMaterializer::materialize.
    • 

  • Outcome. fn classify(results: &AdaptResults, meta: &RunMeta) -> Outcome (below) feeds the header and the checks panel. draw_complete() lists scaffold.files, milestones_created (with reused), issues_created, issues_skipped and tech_debt_issue.
    • 

  • Frame. Draw through the shared ds::wizard_frame used by the issue and milestone wizards. Path editing uses the existing TextAreaField in single-line mode. The Activity Log pane goes away, per the shell rules.
    • 



// adapt/types.rs — refuse to resume a cache that belongs to another run.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
pub struct CacheKey { pub root: PathBuf, pub model: String, pub stop_after: StopAfter }

pub enum Resume { Fresh, From(AdaptStep), Mismatch(Vec<&'static str>) }

impl AdaptResults {
    pub fn resume_for(&self, key: &CacheKey, cached: Option<&CacheKey>) -> Resume {
        let Some(c) = cached else { return Resume::Fresh };
        let mut diff = Vec::new();
        if c.root != key.root { diff.push("project root"); }
        if c.model != key.model { diff.push("model"); }
        if c.stop_after != key.stop_after { diff.push("stop after"); }
        if diff.is_empty() { Resume::From(self.resume_step()) } else { Resume::Mismatch(diff) }
    }
}


// adapt/outcome.rs (proposed) — never print "success" over an implausible result.
pub enum Outcome { Finished, UpToDate, LooksWrong(Vec<Check>), Failed(AdaptError) }

pub fn classify(r: &AdaptResults, meta: &RunMeta) -> Outcome {
    let mut bad = Vec::new();
    if let (Some(p), Some(rep)) = (&r.profile, &r.report) {
        if p.source_stats.total_files >= 50 && rep.modules.is_empty() {
            bad.push(Check::warn("Analysis", format!("0 modules for {} files", p.source_stats.total_files)));
        }
    }
    if meta.claude_calls > 0 && r.plan.as_ref().is_some_and(|p| p.milestones.is_empty()) {
        bad.push(Check::warn("Plan", "0 milestones"));
    }
    if !bad.is_empty() { return Outcome::LooksWrong(bad); }
    match &r.materialize {
        Some(m) if m.issues_created.is_empty() && !m.issues_skipped.is_empty() => Outcome::UpToDate,
        _ => Outcome::Finished,
    }
}

// src/tui/screens/pr_review/gate.rs (proposed) — one gate for manual merge, the dialog and auto_merge.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MergeBlocker {
    ChecksFailing(Vec<String>),  // names of failed runs
    ChecksRunning(usize),
    ChecksHeld,                  // workflows awaiting maintainer approval
    Conflicting,
    ChangesRequested,
    Draft,
    MergeStateUnknown,
}

pub fn merge_gate(pr: &PullRequest, checks: &[CheckRun]) -> Result<(), Vec<MergeBlocker>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let failed: Vec<String> = checks.iter().filter(|c| matches!(c.conclusion,
        CheckConclusion::Failure | CheckConclusion::TimedOut | CheckConclusion::Cancelled
        | CheckConclusion::StartupFailure | CheckConclusion::ActionRequired))
        .map(|c| c.name.clone()).collect();
    if !failed.is_empty() { out.push(MergeBlocker::ChecksFailing(failed)); }
    let running = checks.iter().filter(|c| c.status != CheckStatus::Completed).count();
    if running > 0 { out.push(MergeBlocker::ChecksRunning(running)); }
    match pr.merge_state {
        MergeState::Conflicting => out.push(MergeBlocker::Conflicting),
        MergeState::Unknown => out.push(MergeBlocker::MergeStateUnknown),
        MergeState::Clean | MergeState::Blocked => {}
    }
    if pr.review_decision == Some(ReviewDecision::ChangesRequested) { out.push(MergeBlocker::ChangesRequested); }
    if pr.draft { out.push(MergeBlocker::Draft); }
    if out.is_empty() { Ok(()) } else { Err(out) } // no override parameter, on purpose
}


// provider/github/gh_argv.rs — every mutating builder takes the repo; merge pins the head commit.
pub(crate) fn build_submit_pr_review_argv(pr: u64, event: ReviewEvent, body: &str, repo: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut argv = vec!["pr".into(), "review".into(), pr.to_string(), format!("--{}", event.as_gh_arg())];
    if !body.is_empty() { argv.extend(["--body".into(), body.into()]); }
    append_repo(&mut argv, repo); // was missing: reviews went to the cwd repo
    argv
}

pub(crate) fn build_merge_pr_argv(pr: u64, method: &MergeMethod, head_sha: &str, repo: Option<&str>) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut argv = vec!["pr".into(), "merge".into(), pr.to_string(), method.flag().into(),
        "--delete-branch".into(), "--match-head-commit".into(), head_sha.into()];
    append_repo(&mut argv, repo);
    argv
}

#[test]
fn every_mutating_argv_carries_repo() {
    let r = Some("owner/repo");
    for argv in [
        build_submit_pr_review_argv(1, ReviewEvent::Comment, "x", r),
        build_merge_pr_argv(1, &MergeMethod::Squash, "abc1234", r),
    ] {
        assert!(argv.windows(2).any(|w| w[0] == "--repo" && w[1] == "owner/repo"), "{argv:?}");
    }
}

Session header session::header new

Gates already running are separate processes and keep going.

Implementation


    

  • Screen. New TuiMode::Session { id, view: SessionView } (proposed) with SessionView::{Detail, Output, Log, Gates, Events}. It replaces Detail(id), Fullscreen(id), LogViewer(id), CallLog(id) and GateOutputViewer(id); the old variants stay as constructors that set the view, so navigate_to callers and the nav stack keep working.
    • 

  • Detail (detail.rs): reuse Dashboard's pipeline_stage and section renderers so the pane and the full screen cannot drift. Files come from files_touched and per-file stats from the diff (proposed); the ! marker comes from file_claims.conflicts_for_session, which is already passed in. Drop "Phase: UNKNOWN" when progress_tracker has no entry.
    • 

  • Output (fullscreen.rs): render call_log entries (assistant messages, tool use and results) as rows instead of only last_message; keep OutputViewState { offset, follow, open: HashSet<usize> } per session id. follow turns off on any upward scroll and back on with End.
    • 

  • Log (log_viewer.rs): parse each line once in LogViewerCache into (DateTime<Utc>, Kind, &str) and format with with_timezone(&Local); the kind filter is a u8 bitmask.
    • 

  • Deps (dep_graph.rs): build the tree from WorkAssigner::all_items() and blocked_by; critical path = longest chain of unfinished items (memoised DFS); "holds up" = size of the transitive downstream set. On Wide, layer by longest path from a root and draw edges on a Canvas or with box-drawing; file overlap comes from agent_graph::model::build_graph edges where one file has more than one agent.
    • 

  • Switcher (session_switcher.rs): handle KeyCode::Char and Backspace; sort by urgency; keep selection by Uuid, not index.
    • 

  • Run summary: merge session_summary.rs and the completion overlay into one screen fed by CompletionSummaryData; the "any key dismisses" clearing in handle_completion_summary goes away.
    • 

  • Hints and keymap: mode_hints.rs drops the Overview hint set and the SessionAware F-bar (F9/F10). The keymap registry test adds the session scope (fails on case twins and on an inner key shadowing an outer one).
    • 



// app/session_lifecycle.rs (proposed): pause one session and make the status say so.
#[cfg(unix)]
pub fn toggle_pause(&mut self, id: uuid::Uuid) -> Option<SessionStatus> {
    let managed = self.pool.get_active_mut(id)?;
    let (to, reason) = match managed.session.status {
        SessionStatus::Running => (SessionStatus::Paused, TransitionReason::UserPause),
        SessionStatus::Paused => (SessionStatus::Running, TransitionReason::UserResume),
        _ => return None, // footer shows "p ⊘ only while running"
    };
    let sent = if to == SessionStatus::Paused { managed.pause() } else { managed.resume() };
    if sent.is_ok() {
        let _ = managed.session.transition_to(to, reason);
        let label = session_label(&managed.session);
        self.toast = Some(Toast::undoable(format!("{} {label}", if to == SessionStatus::Paused { "Paused" } else { "Resumed" }),
                                          UndoAction::TogglePause(id)));
        self.sync_state();
    }
    Some(to)
}


// session_switcher.rs: make the existing filter reachable and rank like Home's attention queue.
fn urgency(s: &Session) -> u8 {
    use SessionStatus::*;
    match s.status {
        FailedGates | Errored => 0,
        NeedsReview => 1,
        NeedsPr | CiFix | ConflictFix => 2,
        Running | GatesRunning | Spawning | Retrying | Stalled | Paused | Interactive | Queued => 3,
        Completed | Killed => 4,
    }
}

pub fn handle_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent, sessions: &[&Session]) -> Option<SwitcherTarget> {
    match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char(c) if !key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => { self.filter_text.push(c); self.selected = None; }
        KeyCode::Backspace => { self.filter_text.pop(); self.selected = None; }
        KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Down => self.step(key.code == KeyCode::Down, sessions),
        KeyCode::Enter => return self.selected_session(sessions).map(switcher_target),
        _ => {}
    }
    None
}
// filtered_sessions(): same predicate as today, then .sort_by_key(|s| (urgency(s), Reverse(s.started_at))).
// `selected: Option<Uuid>` replaces `selected_index`, so a session finishing mid-pick can't shift the target.

02.14Usage: cost, tokens and TurboQuant


One question: what is this costing, and how do I spend less? v0.31.8 splits the answer across three screens (Cost, Tokens, TurboQuant) that do not say which sessions they count, show $-0.00 and $0.0000, and never mention quota, routing or what the cap does. The redesign is two Dashboard sub-views, c Cost and t Tokens. They share one scope line (this run), one set of words for estimates, and a Spend less panel built from the run's own numbers. TurboQuant becomes a KPI tile and a panel inside Tokens, as the Dashboard redesign decided.

Why two views, not three screens


    

  • Cost answers "how much and how fast"; Tokens answers "why". Both cover the same sessions and the same scope, so the selected row is kept when you switch between c and t (proposed).
    • 

  • TurboQuant is a token metric. Its honest number (fork-handoff compression) is small next to prompt caching (about $0.03 vs $12.40 in the busy run here). Putting the two side by side in Tokens shows that comparison without editorialising.
    • 

  • History belongs to Stats. Project stats (02.4) owns "Spend · 30 days". This screen owns "this run", which is what the cap acts on. The strip names both so the numbers never look contradictory.
    • 




Screen components


Budget panel usage::budget_panel




Left: normal run. Right: near cap, focused. The threshold list is generated from BudgetConfig (total_usd, per_session_usd, alert_threshold_pct), so it is correct for any config. When a live session is close to its own cap, the panel names it and gives minutes left at that session's rate.



Quota windows usage::quota_panel




Reads App.quota.windows (no fetch in draw). With [quota] enabled = false the panel says so and names the setting instead of showing -. Stale data (ProviderWindows.stale) is drawn muted with its age, because routing already ignores it (quota/routing.rs).



TurboQuant savings usage::tq_panel




Top left: unfocused, narrow. Bottom left: TurboQuant off, so the row reads "would save" and the key turns it on. Right: focused with per-session rows and settings. The estimate's ratio is the same 4.0× for every session because the formula is a fixed ratio. The screen shows that plainly instead of hiding it.



Spend less usage::levers new




Each lever is computed, never canned. Model swap = opus spend ÷ 5 (sonnet's rates are exactly one fifth of opus in claude_pricing.rs). Failing spend = cost of sessions in FailedGates/Errored. Cache = cache_read × (input − cache_read rate). At most three levers, ranked: cap risk, unpriced sessions, model share, failed spend, cache. Every lever ends with the key that acts on it.

// src/tui/ds/money.rs (proposed) — the only way any screen prints dollars.
pub enum Usd { Known(f64), Unpriced }

pub fn money(v: Usd) -> String {
    match v {
        Usd::Unpriced => "$?".into(),
        Usd::Known(x) => {
            let x = crate::budget::sanitize::sanitize_cost(x) + 0.0; // NaN, negatives and -0.0 → 0.0
            if x == 0.0 { "$0.00".into() }
            else if x < 0.01 { "<$0.01".into() }
            else { format!("${x:.2}") }
        }
    }
}

/// What the Budget panel lists under "What happens". Generated from config so it never drifts.
pub fn thresholds(cfg: &BudgetConfig) -> [(f64, &'static str); 3] {
    [
        (cfg.total_usd * f64::from(cfg.alert_threshold_pct) / 100.0, "banner, one log line"),
        (cfg.per_session_usd, "one session: it stops (errored)"),
        (cfg.total_usd, "all agents killed, maestro exits"), // app/budget.rs: running = false
    ]
}


// src/tui/screens/dashboard/cost.rs (proposed) — Wide layout with ratatui 0.29.
pub fn draw_cost(f: &mut Frame, area: Rect, app: &App, view: &CostView, t: &Theme) {
    let bp = Breakpoint::from_area(area).unwrap_or(Breakpoint::Compact);
    let [strip, kpis, body] = Layout::vertical([
        Constraint::Length(1), Constraint::Length(4), Constraint::Fill(1),
    ]).areas(area);
    draw_view_strip(f, strip, DashboardView::Cost, scope_line(app), t);
    if bp == Breakpoint::Compact {
        draw_budget_strip(f, kpis, app, t); // spent gauge, rate, time to cap · 5h/7d · what happens at cap
        return draw_compact(f, body, app, view, t);
    }
    let n = if bp == Breakpoint::Wide { 4 } else { 3 };
    for (tile, rect) in cost_tiles(app).iter().zip(Layout::horizontal(vec![Constraint::Fill(1); n]).split(kpis).iter()) {
        ds::kpi_tile(f, *rect, tile, t);
    }
    let side = if bp == Breakpoint::Wide { 58 } else { 48 };
    let [list, right] = Layout::horizontal([Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(side)]).areas(body);
    draw_spend_by_session(f, list, app, view.focus == Panel::Sessions, t);
    let [budget, quota, levers] = Layout::vertical([
        Constraint::Length(12), Constraint::Length(8), Constraint::Fill(1),
    ]).areas(right);
    draw_budget(f, budget, app, t);
    draw_quota(f, quota, &app.quota, t);   // windows already in memory; draw never fetches
    draw_levers(f, levers, &levers::compute(app), t);
}

02.15Settings


Settings edits maestro.toml. In v0.31.8 it draws each setting as a bare key and a value, even though every FieldSchema in src/config/schema/ already has a label, help text, default and range. The redesign draws all of that, marks dangerous and restart-only settings, searches every setting rather than category names, and writes the file only after you have seen a diff and pressed an armed save.


What the code does today: 15 tabs (SettingsTab::ALL), each built from the schema registry by schema_tab::build::from_schema, plus four hand-made rows (bypass toggle, default-provider dropdown, live_preview, caveman_mode). Ctrl+s runs the validators, then Config::save, which is comment-preserving (toml_edit overlay) and atomic for an existing file. The App then applies the new config live (ScreenAction::UpdateConfig in screen_dispatch.rs), except the pool size, which needs a restart. There is no user-level config tier: maestro reads ./maestro.toml or ./.maestro/config.toml from the working directory only (docs/configuration.md), so "scope" below means which file a value lives in, not user vs repo.

Implementation


    

  • Labels and help. SettingsField gains schema: Option<&'static FieldSchema> and key: String (full path). from_schema already has both; today it keeps only the dotted key as the widget label. draw_fields renders schema.label, the control, the range from FieldKind, the default from DefaultValue and schema.help.
    • 

  • Field metadata (proposed): a meta(key) -> FieldMeta lookup beside the schema (keeps FieldSchema const and the docs generator unchanged): danger kind, when it applies, file, unit. Validators move from (tab, index) keys to key paths.
    • 

  • Pending changes. Compare toml::Value::try_from(&original_config) with the current config by key path; the review text is Config::save_into_str(original_text) diffed line by line against the file on disk, so the diff shows exactly what the comment-preserving writer will produce. A changed file on disk since load blocks the save and offers r.
    • 

  • Save. Ctrl+s sets review: Some(Armed) instead of calling save_config. screen_dispatch.rs keeps applying UpdateConfig; the max_concurrent_changed special case becomes Applies::Restart on the row. Log the bypass source as settings (typed CONFIRM).
    • 

  • Project actions return ScreenAction::PreviewResetFromDetection first (runs render_or_merge and shows keys_added/keys_preserved), then write with io::atomic_write on the armed second ⏎, keeping unsaved edits or refusing while dirty.
    • 

  • Input. Delete the tab-level a/d/u arm in input.rs; RemoveConfirmModal goes, replaced by staged delete plus UndoBuffer (already 5s, matching the toast). Tab/BackTab move focus; [ ] call next_tab/prev_tab over the grouped order.
    • 

  • Search replaces sidebar_search with a query over every SettingsField (label + key); sidebar_visible_indices becomes "categories with hits".
    • 

  • Theme. Drop the live_preview row: focusing tui.theme.preset emits PreviewTheme(Some(..)), leaving the row or Esc emits PreviewTheme(None). The preview panel reuses the real status bar, panel, chips and gauge.
    • 



// src/tui/screens/settings/meta.rs (proposed)
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Applies { Live, NewSessions, Restart, OnToggle }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Danger { Bypass, SpendCap, Shell }

pub struct FieldMeta { pub danger: Option<Danger>, pub applies: Applies, pub file: &'static str }

pub fn meta(key: &str) -> FieldMeta {
    use Applies::*;
    let (danger, applies) = match key {
        "sessions.permission_mode" => (Some(Danger::Bypass), NewSessions),
        "budget.total_usd" | "budget.per_session_usd" => (Some(Danger::SpendCap), Live),
        "gates.test_command" | "review.command" => (Some(Danger::Shell), Live),
        k if k.ends_with(".run") || k.ends_with(".command") || k.ends_with(".extra_args") => (Some(Danger::Shell), Live),
        "sessions.max_concurrent" => (None, Restart),
        k if k.starts_with("agents.") || k.starts_with("modes.") => (None, NewSessions),
        "behavior.caveman_mode" => (None, OnToggle),
        _ => (None, Live),
    };
    let file = if key == "behavior.caveman_mode" { ".claude/settings.json" } else { "maestro.toml" };
    FieldMeta { danger, applies, file }
}

/// The token the operator must type to stage a change, or None when the change is safe
/// (bypass off, a lower cap, reverting a command).
pub fn confirm_token(d: Danger, before: &toml::Value, after: &toml::Value) -> Option<String> {
    match d {
        Danger::Bypass => (after.as_str() == Some("bypassPermissions")).then(|| "CONFIRM".into()),
        Danger::SpendCap => match (before.as_float(), after.as_float()) {
            (Some(b), Some(a)) if a > b => Some(format!("{a:.0}")),
            _ => None,
        },
        Danger::Shell => after.as_str().filter(|s| !s.is_empty())
            .and_then(|s| s.split_whitespace().next()).map(str::to_owned),
    }
}


// src/tui/screens/settings/input.rs — Ctrl+S becomes review, then armed save
const ARM_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(3);

fn on_save_chord(&mut self, now: Instant) -> ScreenAction {
    if let Some(first) = self.first_error_key() {
        self.focus_key(&first);                   // blocked: jump to the first invalid row
        return ScreenAction::None;
    }
    if self.pending_changes().is_empty() { return ScreenAction::None; }
    match self.review.take() {
        Some(Review { armed_at: Some(t), .. }) if now.duration_since(t) <= ARM_WINDOW => {
            match self.save_config() {               // existing: validate, Config::save, reset original
                Ok(()) => ScreenAction::UpdateConfig(Box::new(self.config.clone())),
                Err(e) => self.save_failed(e),       // "nothing written"; edits stay staged
            }
        }
        Some(mut r) => { r.armed_at = Some(now); self.review = Some(r); ScreenAction::None }
        None => { self.review = Some(Review::open(self, now)); ScreenAction::None } // opens armed
    }
}

02.16Teams: entry, Compose, Manage


Teams is where you choose, build and maintain team presets: a shape (primitive) plus an agent for each role. The core change: the centred c / l / m menu becomes an overview of every preset across the three tiers, each shown on one preset card. The card shows the shape as a flow, each role's agent with health, model and price, and an estimate per issue. Compose becomes a four-step wizard in the shared frame. It ends in an armed write that shows the exact file and TOML.


Already covered:
Home Actions t Teams (02): this screen is that entry's destination. Teams links to it and does not redraw it; Home's row keeps its label.
Wizard frame (02.2 Create issue, 02.3 Create milestone, 02.11 Adapt): reused as is. That means the CrumbBar with draft saved, stepper(), the Wide checklistPanel('Draft') and the Regular/Compact readyStrip. The guidance panel under the checklist is replaced by the live preset card.
armedBar (kit) and the TypedConfirm look (02.15 Settings dangerBox, 02.1 Dashboard kill dialog): reused for Save and Delete.
launchDialogKit SPEND / WHERE (02.8): not drawn here, because Compose and Manage never spawn anything. ⏎ on a preset hands it to Teams Launch (02.17), which reuses those rows.
Money wording $? / <$0.01 (02.14 Usage): reused for unpriced agents.
Milestones run queue (02.9) open question, "use the Team launch Scheduler for parallel waves": answered under Implementation. Share the plan (dag::topo_levels), not today's executor. team_runner marks a level done when its sessions spawn, and it plans one level because blocked_by is empty, so it is not yet a better executor than QueueExecutor. Presets reach a milestone only through Teams Launch.
Session rail epic #1183–#1189 (plans/tui-sidebar-rings): does not overlap.

Single-pass needs nothing but dispatches Reviewer. Fan-out needs reviewer but dispatches implementer, reviewer and docs. dispatch::binding_for then fails with no binding for role Triager. The built-ins default-researcher and default-docs and the project's issue-sanitizer all bind the wrong role.Compose validates a preset that cannot run under maestro team launch --yes. 2"Healthy agents" is not a health check. populate_team_wizard_data seeds every configured agent as available: true with "seeded (real health check pending)". If the check were real, the agent would just disappear with no reason given.HIGHRun doctor::run_health_check when Roles opens. Show every agent with ● ok, ✗ down plus its reason, or ○ unchecked. 3Deleting a parent preset breaks every team. Loader::resolve() returns Err on extends missing parent, and populate_team_wizard_data turns that into an empty map. // orchestration/types.rs (proposed): one source of truth for which roles a shape runs
impl Primitive {
    pub fn dispatched_roles(self) -> &'static [TeamRole] {
        match self {
            Self::Pipeline | Self::FanOut => &[TeamRole::Implementer, TeamRole::Reviewer, TeamRole::Docs],
            Self::SinglePass => &[TeamRole::Reviewer],
            Self::VerdictOnly => &[TeamRole::Triager],
        }
    }
    pub fn required_roles(self) -> &'static [TeamRole] { self.dispatched_roles() }
}


// widgets/preset_card.rs (proposed), ratatui 0.29
pub fn draw_preset_card(f: &mut Frame, area: Rect, theme: &Theme, team: &ResolvedTeam,
                        health: &PreflightCache, focused: bool) {
    let title = Line::from(vec![
        Span::styled(sanitize_for_terminal(&team.name), theme.title_style()),
        Span::raw(" "), tier_chip(team.source_tier, theme),
    ]);
    let block = theme.styled_block_plain(focused).title(title)
        .title(Line::from(team.primitive.label()).right_aligned());
    let inner = block.inner(area); f.render_widget(block, area);
    let mut lines = vec![shape_line(team, health, theme), Line::default()];
    for role in team.primitive.dispatched_roles() {
        lines.push(match team.bindings.get(role) {
            Some(b) => role_row(role, &b.agent, health.by_agent.get(&b.agent), theme, inner.width),
            None => unbound_row(role, theme),           // "✗ unbound · launch fails here"
        });
    }
    lines.push(l2_row(health, theme));
    lines.push(est_line(estimate_cost_usd(team, 1, 200), theme));
    f.render_widget(Paragraph::new(lines), inner);
}

02.17Teams: Launch


Launch runs a team preset on one issue, a set of issues or a milestone. v0.31.8 spreads that over eight one-item screens. The team list shows names only, issue suggestions show bare numbers, and the plan reads ≈ $0.0000 (rough estimate, ±50%). Two presses of ⏎ later, agents are spending money. The redesign has three steps (Team · Input · Plan & launch). Teams appear as cards that say what each one does and what will actually run. Every input issue shows its readiness. The plan is drawn as waves of lanes with stages, and its cost line is honest: it gives the exact worst case against the budget left and says when no estimate exists. The launch dialog follows the shared launch dialog.



Already covered:

    

  • 02.8 Issues, launchDialogKit: reused by copy. The team launch dialog keeps its SPEND, WHERE, warning and button rows word for word. It replaces INSTRUCTIONS and MODE with WHAT (waves) and TEAM (stages, runs-as agent), because team sessions take no instructions and always run Autonomous → PR.
    • 

  • 02.9 Milestones, Run queue (waves, WILL RUN / NOT INCLUDED, readiness notes, run bar): reused. The Input step's milestone list and the plan's wave lanes use the same data, row notes and wording, so one milestone reads the same on both screens. 02.9's open question was "use the Team launch Scheduler for parallel waves". This screen answers it: Scheduler::from_input already builds the waves, but in v0.31.8 it gets no dependency edges (finding 6), so both screens need the same fix to IssueMeta.blocked_by.
    • 

  • 02.16 Teams (team_compose), presetCard: reused. The sidebar draws team_compose's card (shape line, one row per dispatched role, L2 row, tier chip). Until that file lands, a local copy with the same signature stands in. The picker entries are a 3-row summary of the same data. This screen hides the card's est line (noEst) because it uses the honest cost line instead (open question 1).
    • 

  • 02 Home, Actions t Teams: links to. Home t → Teams → ⏎ on a preset opens this screen with the team already picked.
    •

Audit of v0.31.8




#FindingImpactSevFix



1LaunchStep has 8 entries, and the header counts all of them (Step 1/8), including Executing, LaunchSuccess and LaunchFailed. PlanPreview and Confirm are separate steps, but Confirm only repeats "N issues across L levels". Launching one issue takes 5 presses of ⏎.The wizard feels twice as long as it is. The second ⏎ becomes a reflex, and that is the one that spends money.HIGH3 steps. The results are states, not steps. Plan and Confirm merge into one step, followed by a launch dialog that states sessions, worst case and worktrees.


2estimate_cost_usd (orchestration/cost.rs) counts prompt tokens only: 200 (L2) + role prompt + 800 context + 900 retry tokens at $6/M. That comes to $0.0012 per single-pass issue and $0.026 per pipeline issue. Idea inbox plans 0 issues, so the screenshot shows $0.0000. {:.4} prints four decimals next to "rough, ±50%".A real session costs dollars and stops at per_session_usd ($5). The screen understates the spend by two to three orders of magnitude, right before the user confirms.HIGHShow the exact bound (n × per-session cap) against the budget left. Show an estimate only when there is run history; otherwise say not available. Use money(), never 4 decimals.


3What runs is not what the preset says. team_runner::run_team spawns one ordinary session per issue (TuiDataEvent::Issue, the same path as Issues ⏎). The agent comes from the implementer binding, else the app default. Reviewer, docs and triager roles are never dispatched (scheduler.rs agent_for_issue, "R1").default-reviewer and default-triager launch implementation sessions that open PRs. The team picker gives no hint of this.HIGHEach card says runs as 1 <agent> session per issue. Preflight carries a ! Role routing warning. The launch dialog states it once more.


4The team picker lists sorted names (draw_launch_team_picker) even though ResolvedTeam has the primitive, bindings, tier and min_agents. Preflight runs only at the plan step, so a preset that cannot launch is found two steps later.Users pick by name, with no idea what each team does or costs.MEDEach team gets a card: what it does, roles → agents, runs-as agent, cost history and a ready/⊘ state. Presets that cannot launch are marked on the picker, and ⏎ on them explains why.


5Input kinds are bare enum names. From the picker, IssueSet and Milestone silently do nothing when manual_issues is empty (launch_commit_input returns), so they work only when the wizard was opened from Milestones t. IdeaInbox plans 0 issues, passes preflight, and fails at dispatch with "Scheduler produced an empty plan".Two of the four options are dead ends, and the wizard gives no reason.HIGHEach kind gets a one-line explanation. Milestone and Issues open their own pickers. Idea inbox is drawn ⊘ with the reason until the triager input exists.


6Wizard issue metas are built with blocked_by: Vec::new() (data_handler.rs:140). Every plan is a single level, auto_expand never adds a blocker, and the OpenExternalDep preflight never fires.The DAG scheduler shown in the plan is decoration. Blocked issues launch alongside their blockers.HIGHParse ## Blocked By from the issue body (same code as 02.9). The Input step then shows waits / blocked, and the plan shows real waves.


7The issue step accepts digits only and suggests the first 5 open numbers that start with the buffer, with no titles. The screenshot's 11 suggests #1102…#1184. ⏎ accepts any number > 0, even one that is not an open issue.Users must know issue numbers by heart, and a typo launches on the wrong issue.MEDA search field over title and number. Matches show milestone, status and claim. A number that is not an open issue is shown as such and cannot be picked.


8In run_team, a level "succeeds" once its sessions have spawned (issue fetched and queued). Level 2 starts seconds after level 1 instead of after it finishes. max_parallel is fixed at 3 in with_entry and bounds only the spawn semaphore.The "Level 0 / Level 1" order in the preview does not hold at run time.MEDThe plan states this, and the result panel says "spawned ≠ finished". Proposed: gate each wave on the previous wave reaching a terminal state.


9Agent health is seeded available: true ("real health check pending", screen_dispatch.rs). The status bar repeats [l] Launch [m] Manage [Enter] Confirm. The issue panel repeats the footer hints. A red Select a team shows before any input.The preflight looks stronger than it is. Every hint appears two or three times, and the user starts with an error they did not cause.LOWHealth shows as ! not checked. Hints appear only in the footer. Validation shows after a ⏎ on an invalid step, never on entry.





Reimagined




    

  1. Wizard frame: same as the issue, milestone and adapt wizards. Home › Teams › Launch with a launch ledger on the right (○ nothing launched yet, then ● 4 sessions launched), a 3-step stepper, and the choices so far on the right of the stepper row. On Wide the right column holds Preflight and the team card. On Regular and Compact it becomes a one-line readyStrip.
    2. 

  2. Team cards, grouped by tier. Row 1 shows name, primitive, tier and ✓ ready or ⊘ reason. Row 2 says what the team does. Row 3 shows roles → agents, runs as (the agent the runtime will really use) and cost history. Presets that cannot launch stay visible, with the reason.
    3. 

  3. Run on: four input kinds, each with one line on what it means. Idea inbox is ⊘ with the reason. When the screen is opened from Issues or Milestones t, the panel says from Milestones t and Input is already ✓.

    5.

    6. 

  6. Run plan: the stage chain once (① implementer claude ─▶ ② reviewer claude ─▶ ③ docs claude), then one lane per issue grouped by wave, each with its cap and readiness note. The issues left out are listed with their reasons. Two ! lines state what v0.31.8 does differently (one session per lane; wave 2 starts when wave 1 has spawned).
    7. 

  7. Launch bar: sessions, waves, at-once count against the config limits, an estimate that may say "not available", and an exact worst case gauge against the budget left. ⏎ only opens the dialog.
    8. 

  8. Launch dialog: WHAT (waves), TEAM (stages, runs as), SPEND, WHERE and warnings. When the worst case exceeds the budget left, it says what happens at the cap (every agent stops and maestro exits) and offers w wave 1 only. ⏎ is then armed: press it twice within 3 s.
    9. 

  9. Result: one row per issue (✓ spawned · ✗ failed · ○ skipped), a double-border header when anything failed, r to re-plan only the failed and skipped issues, and ⏎ to Dashboard to follow the sessions.

// launch.rs — honest cost line (proposed)
let worst = plan.final_count as f64 * cfg.budget.per_session_usd;
let left = (cfg.budget.total_usd - app.total_cost).max(0.0);
let ratio = (app.total_cost + worst) / cfg.budget.total_usd;
let est = match history.median_for_team(&plan.team_name) {
    Some(m) if m.runs >= 3 => Span::raw(format!("~{} ({} × median {}, {} runs)",
        money(m.median * plan.final_count as f64), plan.final_count, money(m.median), m.runs)),
    _ => Span::styled("not available", theme.text_secondary),
};
let over = worst > left;               // drives the armed ⏎ and the "w wave 1 only" offer

02.18Fleet board


The Fleet board lists every Claude Code conversation on this machine: this run's maestro sessions, sessions you adopted, conversations you ran yourself in any project, and transcripts left by earlier maestro runs. Use it to find a conversation, see where it lives and whether it may still be running, then open it (maestro sessions) or adopt it (outside sessions). The redesign groups rows by project, gives each row a readable title and a state word, says where each row came from in one word instead of two, and treats the transcripts it reads as private.

Transcript row fleet_board::transcript_row new · shared




Signature, also posted in SYNC.md: transcriptRow(b, x, y, w, t, {sel, focus, cols:'grouped'|'flat'|'compact', mask:'off'|'prompts'|'all', hit, cwdCol}). The state field is either a SessionStatus (pool and adopted rows, using the exact STATUS glyph and word that Home, Dashboard and the switcher use) or an outside-conversation state: ● live? (mtime inside the 10-minute quiet period; the question mark is honest, since mtime is the only liveness signal and #1067 rules out a ps sweep), ○ idle, or ⊘ cwd gone. Source is one word. Compact width keeps the glyph and a 3-letter source, so state is never colour alone. A selected row in an unfocused list keeps ▌ in accent without the fill. Adopt session (02.19) uses the same function.



Title cleaning discovery::clean_title proposed




The left column is what v0.31.8 would show as the title. Examples are invented. Rules, in order: 1. last ai-title wins (already true). 2. Skip user entries with isMeta: true, entries that start with <local-command-caveat> or <local-command-stdout>, and housekeeping commands (/clear /model /compact /resume /login /config /cost /help /status /exit). 3. Any other <command-name> becomes /name args with source command. 4. Strip <system-reminder> and other tag blocks, turn [Image …] into [image], drop leading #, and collapse whitespace. 5. If nothing is left, show (no prompt yet). The result still goes through sanitize_for_terminal at the render sink.
