// rows.rs (proposed): one place decides the row's state word, shared with adopt_picker.
pub enum RowState { Pool(SessionStatus), LiveMaybe, Idle, CwdGone }

impl RowState {
    pub fn of_transcript(t: &DiscoveredSession, now: SystemTime) -> Self {
        if !t.cwd.is_dir() { return Self::CwdGone; }
        if is_live_at(t.last_active, now) { Self::LiveMaybe } else { Self::Idle }
    }
    /// Glyph + word + colour, never colour alone (icons::get honours MAESTRO_ASCII_ICONS;
    /// the IconId names below are illustrative, map them to existing ids).
    pub fn chip(&self, theme: &Theme) -> [Span<'static>; 2] {
        let (icon, word, color) = match self {
            Self::Pool(s) => (status_icon(*s), s.label(), theme.status_color(*s)),
            Self::LiveMaybe => (IconId::Dot, "live?", theme.accent_warning),
            Self::Idle => (IconId::Circle, "idle", theme.text_muted),
            Self::CwdGone => (IconId::Blocked, "cwd gone", theme.text_muted),
        };
        [Span::styled(format!("{} ", icons::get(icon)), Style::default().fg(color)),
         Span::styled(format!("{word:<13}"), Style::default().fg(color))]
    }
}


// headless.rs: helper runs must not leave adoptable transcripts behind.
pub(super) fn build_text_args(request: &AgentRequest) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut args = vec!["--print".into(), "--no-session-persistence".into(), // (proposed)
                        "--output-format".into(), "text".into()];
    // … model, -p prompt unchanged
    args
}

02.19Adopt session


Adopt session takes a Claude Code conversation you started outside maestro and continues it as a maestro Interactive session (claude --resume <id> in the conversation's own folder). v0.31.8 shows every transcript on the machine as one flat list of raw first lines, and Enter adopts at once. The redesign puts this repo first, cleans the titles, says on each row whether it can be adopted and why not, previews the last turns, and asks once before adopting. The confirm states the folder, branch, model, spend, permissions and what happens to the original conversation.

// src/session/adopt.rs (proposed) — one source of truth for "can this row be adopted?"
pub enum Adoptability {
    Ready { quiet: bool },              // quiet = outside ADOPT_QUIET_PERIOD
    CwdGone,                            // !cwd.is_dir()
    OpenInPool { session: uuid::Uuid }, // same agent_session_id, status.is_live()
    NothingToResume,                    // no plain prompt and no assistant reply
}

pub fn adoptability(s: &DiscoveredSession, pool: &SessionPool, now: SystemTime) -> Adoptability {
    if !s.has_reply && s.title.from == TitleFrom::None { return Adoptability::NothingToResume; }
    if let Some(open) = pool.live_by_agent_session_id(&s.session_id) {
        return Adoptability::OpenInPool { session: open.id };
    }
    if !s.cwd.is_dir() { return Adoptability::CwdGone; }
    Adoptability::Ready { quiet: !is_live_at(s.last_active, now) }
}


// adopt_picker/draw.rs — group header + rows; transcript_row is Fleet board's shared widget
fn draw_group(f: &mut Frame, area: Rect, y: &mut u16, label: &str, rows: &[&Row], st: &State, theme: &Theme) {
    let head = Line::from(vec![
        Span::styled(label.to_string(), Style::default().fg(theme.text_muted).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
        Span::styled(format!("  {}", rows.len()), Style::default().fg(theme.text_primary).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
    ]);
    f.render_widget(Paragraph::new(head), Rect { y: *y, height: 1, ..area });
    *y += 1;
    for row in rows {
        let selected = st.selected_id.as_deref() == Some(row.session_id.as_str());
        transcript_row(f, Rect { y: *y, height: 1, ..area }, row, selected, st.focus == Focus::List, theme);
        *y += 1;
    }
}

02.20Agent graph


The agent graph answers one question: which agents are touching the same files right now? In v0.31.8 it is a separate mode (TuiMode::AgentGraph) behind g on Overview: a radial picture with role sprites on an inner ring and file names on an outer ring. The redesign keeps the question and drops the separate mode. It becomes the Files lens of the Dashboard Deps view: agents on the left, repo-relative files on the right, braille edges between them, files that two or more agents edit at the top, and one detail panel that says what to do about them.

What it showsA bipartite graph from build_graph(app.pool.all_sessions()): one agent node per session (active, finished and queued), one file node per unique raw path in Session::files_touched, one edge per (session, path).   1. View strip with the lens switch. o Ops · c Cost · t Tokens · g Deps, then lens issues · files  g switch with the active lens reversed. Right side: 6 live · 15 files edited · 1 contested. When the flag is off the files chip reads ⊘ off in [views].
    2. 

  2. Agents column. Dashboard's row: STATUS glyph, #n, name, status word, ✎4 (files it edits). Rows are spread over the height of the file column so edges stay short. In a team run the members sit under a TEAM default-coder · wave 1/2 header, which is itself selectable.
    3. 

  3. Edge band. Braille S-curves (Canvas + Marker::Braille), flat at both ends so they meet the rows. Edges of the selection are accent and bold; edges into a contested file are warning; the rest are muted. Read edges are drawn only with m, dimmed.
    4. 

  4. Files column. Repo-relative paths (worktrees merged), middle-truncated so the file name survives. Sections CONTESTED (2+ editors, always first) · EDITED · READ ONLY (only with m; otherwise + 3 read only · m shows them). A recorded conflict says ✗ conflict 2✎.
    5. 

  5. One detail panel for the selection. File: who holds the claim, who edited after and when, the conflict policy and what it does, and what you can do. Agent: identity (the role sprite, on Wide only, coloured by status), status, role and where the role came from, agent badge (claude/codex) and model, what it is doing now, context, its files. Team: shape line, stage grid by wave, the same-wave overlap warning.
    6. 

  6. File events (Wide, when there is room): edits, claims and conflicts, newest first, from Session.activity_log and conflict_history. Rows for the selection are bold.
    7. 

  7. Footer for the focused column only. File rows: ← agents on it · ⏎ open owner · p pause other. Agent rows: → its files · ⏎ open session · p pause · X kill….
    8. 

  8. Conflict toast when process_file_claim_event records a conflict: file, policy, who holds the claim, p pause #409 · ⏎ show file. It replaces today's ERROR log line as the visible signal; the log line stays.
    9. 

  9. Compact (< 100 cols): no canvas. A tree of agents with their edited files, contested files flagged ! also #409, the contested summary on top, and a 3-line strip for the selection. ASCII icons: no canvas at any width; each file row lists its editors (#407 #409), status uses the bracket codes ([*] [!]), role shows its 3-letter code.

File card agent_graph::file_card new




The place where a conflict turns into an action. Owner first (holds the claim), then who edited after, then readers. The policy line says what maestro already did (warn: logged and notified, both keep running) and points to the setting.

A running TeamRun as roles × waves. The shape line uses team_compose's words. Implementation


    

  • Mode. TuiMode::AgentGraph stays as an alias for one release: navigate_to(AgentGraph) → Dashboard with view: Deps, lens: DepsLens::Files (proposed), still gated by is_agent_graph_enabled() (#527 kept). toggle_agent_graph becomes the lens toggle. mode_hints.rs drops AGENT_GRAPH_HINTS and HINT_OV_GRAPH; the lens hints come from the Dashboard keymap, fitted with fit_hints_to_width.

  • Model (model.rs, extends build_graph): key files with file_claims::repo_relative_key(path, worktree); add EdgeKind::{Edit, Read} — Edit when the file is in file_claims.session_files[id], Read otherwise. Note: claims count Write | Edit but files_touched also counts multiedit; add MultiEdit to the claim match. Drop finished sessions that hold no claim (ADR 001's dim-then-remove, done by state instead of ticks).
    • 

  • Layout (layout.rs, extends the existing Layout trait): ColumnsLayout (proposed) — agents keep pool order, files are ordered contested → edited → read, then by the existing barycenter helper (now on row index, not angle). ConcentricLayout and its tests can be removed; ask the maintainer (see open questions).

  • Render (render.rs): labels are plain Lines in two column Rects, not ctx.print, so label_placement.rs is no longer needed. Only the band is a Canvas (Marker::Braille), each edge an S-curve made of 8 CanvasLine segments. Colours come from Theme (status_color, accent_warning, border_inactive, text_muted); move the lens under src/tui/screens/ or add agent_graph/ to screens_use_theme_colors_only so CI covers it. Panels via styled_block; paths through sanitize_for_terminal.
    • 

  • Identity and states. Agent rows reuse Dashboard's row renderer; provider word and colour from agent_badge::{agent_label, agent_color}; status glyphs through icons::get. personalities.rs stays: the sprite is drawn only in the Wide agent card, role_abbrev in ASCII. 0 agents = EmptyState::idle; 1 agent and no files = the waiting row (replaces empty_state.rs). ASCII (use_nerd_font() == false) and Compact use the tree / owner-list form, no canvas.
    • 

  • Teams. Group rows by app.state.team_runs (TeamRun.plan levels → waves); no NodeKind::Team node in the layout, which removes the index mismatch. Read the primitive from the team definition instead of hard-coding SinglePass.
    • 

  • Docs. Fix the agent_graph_enabled row in docs/configuration.md ("manual lens, not automatic at 2+ sessions"); add the ladder, file card and team card to docs/tui-design-system.md §2 in the same PR; mark ADR 001 "Superseded in part" for the layout section (its own rule says amend the status, not the text).

// layout.rs (proposed): same trait, rows instead of rings. Positions stay in [-1, 1] for the band canvas.
pub(crate) struct ColumnsLayout { pub(crate) agent_rows: usize, pub(crate) file_rows: usize }

impl Layout for ColumnsLayout {
    fn position(&self, nodes: &[GraphNode], edges: &[GraphEdge]) -> Vec<Positioned> {
        let row_y = |i: usize, n: usize| if n <= 1 { 0.0 } else { 1.0 - 2.0 * i as f64 / (n - 1) as f64 };
        let agents: Vec<usize> = idxs(nodes, |k| matches!(k, NodeKind::Agent { .. }));
        let files = order_files(nodes, edges, &agents); // contested → edited → read, then barycenter by row
        let mut out: Vec<Positioned> = agents.iter().enumerate()
            .map(|(r, &i)| Positioned { id_idx: i, x: -1.0, y: row_y(r, self.agent_rows) })
            .chain(files.iter().enumerate()
                .map(|(r, &i)| Positioned { id_idx: i, x: 1.0, y: row_y(r, self.file_rows) }))
            .collect();
        out.sort_by_key(|p| p.id_idx);
        out
    }
}


// render.rs (proposed): the band. Labels live in the column Rects; only edges go on the Canvas.
let band = Canvas::default()
    .marker(Marker::Braille)
    .x_bounds([-1.0, 1.0]).y_bounds([-1.0, 1.0])
    .paint(move |ctx| {
        for e in edges.iter().filter(|e| e.kind == EdgeKind::Edit || show_reads) {
            let (a, f) = (pos[e.from_idx], pos[e.to_idx]);
            let color = if sel.touches(e) { theme.border_active }
                else if contested.contains(&e.to) { theme.accent_warning }
                else { theme.text_muted };
            let smooth = |t: f64| t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t); // flat at both ends
            for s in 0..8 {
                let (t0, t1) = (s as f64 / 8.0, (s + 1) as f64 / 8.0);
                ctx.draw(&CanvasLine {
                    x1: -1.0 + 2.0 * t0, y1: a.y + (f.y - a.y) * smooth(t0),
                    x2: -1.0 + 2.0 * t1, y2: a.y + (f.y - a.y) * smooth(t1),
                    color,
                });
            }
        }
    });
f.render_widget(band, band_rect);

02.21Interaction: chat with an agent


The Interaction screen (TuiMode::Interaction) is where you steer one agent turn by turn: a chat launched from the launch dialog, an adopted outside conversation, or a session you rejoin. In v0.31.8 it shows only the agent's text, sends on ⏎, locks the input while the agent works, shows no cost, and its quit modal says the worktree is kept while the code deletes it. The redesign uses the same transcript format as Session Output, shows every tool call with a status glyph, keeps the composer usable mid-turn, puts the cost of each turn on screen, and asks before anything that deletes work.

The chat transcript uses the same row format and words, plus a per-turn cost rule and folding per turn. Session header and CrumbBar (Dashboard › #1185 home-stack): reused, with › Chat added. Detail / Log / Events: links to them (d). Switcher w: reused; ⏎ on an Interactive row rejoins this screen. Screen components


Turn anatomy interaction::history::build_rows extends




One finished turn with a failed call (folded, ✗ 1 failed stays visible on the row), an opened group (▾, │ gutter), a ▲ push shown even when folded, a ⊘ guarded call selected, the turn rule with its cost, then a live turn with the typing cursor ▌ and a ⣾ now row. Text turns go through sanitize_for_terminal then render_markdown, as today. The cost on the rule is the turn's Completed{cost_usd}; a live turn has no cost yet and the strip says so.



Reply composer and strip interaction::input::composer




States: idle, drafting while the agent works, a multi-line draft, one message queued (QUEUED chip above the box, ⌃Z unqueue), and ended (read-only, says where Esc goes). Only one message can wait: a second ⌃S mid-turn appends to it, so the agent never gets a burst of turns. Follow-up turns cannot carry images (build_followup_request clears them), so ⌃V pastes text only here. The strip under it is the Regular/Compact form of the side panel; the bypass chip is this chat's own permission_mode, not the global flag.



Allow a denied tool, and leaving a live chat interaction::allow new




a on a ⊘ row. It names the exact rule (Bash(git push:*)), its scope (this chat until it ends, maestro.toml untouched), the effect, what stays blocked, and what happens next: the reply box is filled, nothing is sent until you press ⌃S. Typing the command follows the Settings rule for trust-gated commands. Esc keeps it denied. Below: the toast after Esc leaves a working chat. The chat keeps running; w brings you back.



Blocked, failed, stopped, ended interaction::states




Replace the bare "Terminated (user quit). Press any key" banner. Blocked uses the real trust-gate message (maestro trust). A failed turn puts your message back in the reply box so ⌃S resends it (a resend spends money, so it is never on r). A stopped turn says the edits stay. Ended says what was removed and that the PR keeps the commits. Starting (variant start) uses EmptyState::loading with what is fetched and from where.

// interaction/keymap.rs — focus decides who owns a key; ⏎ never sends (proposed)
pub(crate) fn classify(f: Focus, turn: TurnState, ended: bool, code: KeyCode, m: KeyModifiers) -> InteractionIntent {
    use InteractionIntent::*;
    let ctrl = m.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL);
    if ended { return if code == KeyCode::Esc { Back } else { Ignore }; } // no more any-key-leaves
    match (f, code) {
        (Focus::Composer, KeyCode::Char('s')) if ctrl => if turn == TurnState::Streaming { Queue } else { Send },
        (Focus::Composer, KeyCode::Char('p')) if ctrl => DraftPushup,   // fills the editor only
        (Focus::Composer, KeyCode::Char('u')) if ctrl => ClearInput,
        (Focus::Composer, KeyCode::Esc) => FocusTranscript,
        (Focus::Composer, _) => FeedEditor,                             // ⏎, arrows, ⌃J go to the editor
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Esc) => Back,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Tab | KeyCode::Char('i')) => FocusComposer,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Char('X')) => RequestEnd,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Char('S')) => ArmStopTurn,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Char('v')) => OpenDiffReview,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Char('a')) => AllowSelectedTool,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k')) => ScrollUp,
        (Focus::Transcript, KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j')) => ScrollDown,
        _ => Ignore,
    }
}


// tui/app/interaction_pipeline.rs — tool calls reach the chat (proposed)
StreamEvent::ToolUse { tool, file_path, command_preview, .. } => {
    if let Some(turn) = streaming_agent_turn(&mut managed.session.turns) {
        let arg = command_preview.clone().or_else(|| file_path.clone()).unwrap_or_default();
        turn.tools.push(ToolCall {
            wrote_outside: writes_outside_worktree(tool, &arg), // git push, gh pr …, paths outside the tree
            name: tool.clone(), arg: sanitize_for_terminal(&arg), status: ToolStatus::Running,
        });
    }
    Some(TurnEvent::ToolStarted)
}
StreamEvent::ToolResult { is_error, .. } => {
    if let Some(call) = streaming_agent_turn(&mut managed.session.turns).and_then(|t| t.tools.last_mut()) {
        call.status = if *is_error { ToolStatus::Err } else { ToolStatus::Ok };
    }
    None
}

02.22Run loop: queue execution, continuous pause, hollow retry


Three v0.31.8 modes show what happens after you start a batch of agents: QueueExecution (a box over Overview with one progress line), ContinuousPause (a red box when a --continuous run fails) and HollowRetry (a small box when a session "did nothing"). The redesign makes them one screen: the Milestones run plan (02.9), now live. The same groups, rows and Run bar show what is running, what starts next and what it costs so far. When the loop needs you, one decision card states what happened, what each choice does, and what each choice costs. There were no screenshots for this section, so every finding comes from reading the code.

Only the left column changes, from [x] to a live state.

Audit of v0.31.8


No screenshots were supplied. These findings are inferred from the code at 382d211, so each one names the file it comes from.




#FindingImpactSevFix



1The queue does not track its own sessions. QueueExecutor::set_session_id is never called. The loop in tui/mod.rs:869 advances only when app.all_done() (every session in the pool has ended), and it reads success from pool.all_sessions().last(), which is whatever session was added last.Any unrelated running session stalls the queue. An unrelated session that failed (or passed) last decides whether the queue item failed. The queue also runs strictly one at a time, so the plan's "3 at once" never happens (02.9 finding 3).HIGHStore the session id at launch. Report each session's outcome by id. Fill free slots wave by wave (Implementation).


2A hollow run counts as success. detect_hollow_completion keeps status = Completed, and event_handler.rs:203 queues the completion with success: true. So the queue calls mark_success, continuous mode calls on_issue_completed, the completion job runs gates and the PR step, and WorkAssigner::mark_done unblocks dependents. At the same time RetryPolicy relaunches the same issue up to 2 more times.An issue where nothing was done is counted as "done", and the issues it blocks may start. The retries run in parallel with that.HIGHOutcome::Hollow is its own result: not done, nothing unblocked, the row becomes ◐ needs you, and the decision card explains it.


3A running queue cannot be stopped. Esc only leaves the overlay (navigate_back_or_dashboard), and the loop keeps launching. a Abort works only after a failure. It has no confirm and sits one key from s Skip. It marks the queue Finished and leaves the rest Pending, with no message.The only way to stop spending is to kill sessions one by one or quit maestro. The one "stop" key is easy to hit by mistake, and nothing says what it left undone.HIGHh holds the queue (reversible). S opens "Stop the run?": finish the running sessions (default), or kill them (type the count). The dialog says what is kept.


4Every retry is a single lowercase key that starts a paid session and shows no cost: r in QueueExecution, in ContinuousPause and in HollowRetry. HollowRetry's r also goes past the configured limit (the screen shows "Retries: 2/2" in red, and r starts attempt 3 anyway).Reflex spend. The retry is not part of the worst case the user approved at launch.HIGHDecision card: each option shows its cost ($0.00 or est ≥ $0.50 · stops at $5.00) and how it changes the approved worst case. ↑↓ picks, ⏎ confirms. The default option never spends money outside the plan.


5Queue decisions only work inside TuiMode::QueueExecution. mark_failure does not navigate there. If you left with Esc, the queue sits in AwaitingDecision with no prompt anywhere (inferred: no other code path reads that phase).The run stops without telling anyone. This is easy to miss, because leaving the overlay is the normal thing to do.MEDThe waiting item becomes a Home Needs-you row and a ◐ needs you RUN header in the Dashboard Work list, with a toast. The decision card opens from either one.


6ContinuousPause takes its "Error:" text from the newest ERROR among the last 10 global log entries (issue_completion.rs). That may belong to another session. The box has no "what runs next" and no stop key. Esc does nothing. r and s act at once and drop you on Overview.The user decides from an error that may not be about this issue. Stopping continuous mode means quitting maestro.MEDThe card shows that session's own gate result and log lines, what maestro already wrote (the maestro:failed label, the issues that will not run), the next issue, and three options, including "Stop continuous mode".


7Continuous mode spends with nobody watching. maestro run --milestone X --continuous (Flag::ContinuousMode is on by default) forces max_concurrent = 1 and starts the next ready issue on every work tick (about 10 s) after a success. Nothing pauses before [budget].total_usd, and at the cap maestro exits (02.14 fact).An overnight run can only end by failing, by running out of issues, or by the cap stopping maestro.MEDAn "Unattended spend" line (spent, issues left × $5, worst case as a % of the cap). Continuous mode also pauses at the 80% budget alert (proposed).


8HollowRetry says only "completed without performing any observable work" and "Retries: 2/2". It does not show the four checks behind the word (cost $0.00, no files, no tool calls, under 30 s), the earlier attempts, or the cost of trying again. mode_hints.rs advertises Enter Retry · Esc Cancel, but the screen ignores Enter, and Esc means Skip. Skip sets hollow_dismissed, so the prompt never comes back."Hollow" is jargon with no evidence. The footer hint is wrong. A stray Esc drops the decision for good.MEDThe dialog lists the four checks with their values, the 3 attempts and the retry policy, plus a plain "what it usually means" (marked as inferred). Esc means "decide later" and keeps a Needs-you row.


9The queue overlay is one unwrapped line, [✓ #964] [● #969] …, in a box 60% wide. Past about 8 items it is cut off with no sign. The status line names only the current item. The footer always shows r Retry · s Skip, even when they do nothing. A Clear box hides the live sessions behind it.No order, no waves, no cost, and dead hints. You cannot see the sessions you are paying for.MEDA full screen: "Run order" by wave with a state, title and note on every row, the selected session's detail, and a Run bar with progress, spend and worst case. Hints appear only when they work.


10A finished queue opens CompletionSummary on top of everything. Any key dismisses it (02.13 finding 9). Issues that were deferred or skipped are not mentioned.The "what is left" answer disappears with one key press.LOWThe run screen stays, in a finished state: what is still open and why, then ⏎ Run summary (02.13) and R to plan the rest.

Screen components


Live run row run_loop::row extends 02.9 plan row




Same columns as the plan row, so the line under the cursor does not move when the plan goes live. The state is always glyph + word. Session states come from STATUS (● running, ◆ gates running). Queue states are words of their own: ○ next (ready, waiting for a slot), · waits (a blocker or a file overlap is still running), ⊘ skipped, ◐ needs you. Below 96 columns the state column shrinks and "gates running" becomes "gates".



Decision card widgets::decision_card new




One component for every "the loop stopped and needs you" moment: a queue failure, a continuous pause, and a hollow run (as a dialog). It has a heading (what and where), evidence sections, then CHOOSE: a radio list where each option has a one-line result and its price on the right ($0.00 or est ≥ $0.50 · stops at $5.00). If the price does not fit, it moves to the start of the result line. The button repeats the selected option (⏎ Skip #971), and Esc always means "decide later". The default option is the one that does not spend money outside the approved plan. A retry also shows its effect on the plan: worst case $35.00 → $40.00.



Run bar, live run_loop::run_bar extends 02.9 runBar




Same title and place as the plan's Run bar. The worst case is recalculated on every tick: finished rows at their real cost, live and not-started rows at the per-session cap. It can only go down unless you choose a retry. h turns the border yellow and the title right side reads ‖ held · running sessions continue. The button then says what resuming starts (starts #972 in the free slot).



Hollow evidence run_loop::hollow replaces HollowRetryScreen draw




The four rows are exactly Session::detect_hollow_completion: cost_usd == 0, files_touched empty, no tool-call entries in activity_log, elapsed under HOLLOW_DURATION_THRESHOLD_SECS (30). Attempts come from the retry chain (retry_count, last_retry_at). The policy line comes from [sessions.hollow_retry]. A hollow session outside any queue (a prompt run, Issues ⏎) gets the same dialog over the screen you are on. Its Skip says "issue stays open", not "queue continues".

// work/executor.rs (proposed): fill free slots wave by wave, track our own sessions,
// and never let an unrelated session decide an item's outcome.
pub enum Outcome { Done, Failed, Hollow }

impl QueueExecutor {
    /// Items to launch now: pending items whose wave is open and whose in-run blockers are done.
    pub fn next_to_launch(&mut self, free_slots: usize) -> Vec<&QueuedItem> {
        if self.held || self.draining { return Vec::new(); }
        let open_wave = self.items.iter()
            .filter(|i| !matches!(i.state, QueueItemState::Succeeded | QueueItemState::Skipped))
            .map(|i| i.wave).min().unwrap_or(usize::MAX);
        let ready: Vec<usize> = (0..self.items.len())
            .filter(|&k| self.items[k].state == QueueItemState::Pending)
            .filter(|&k| self.items[k].wave <= open_wave + 1 && self.blockers_done(k))
            .take(free_slots.saturating_sub(self.awaiting.len())) // a waiting item keeps its slot empty
            .collect();
        for &k in &ready { self.items[k].state = QueueItemState::Running; }
        ready.into_iter().map(|k| &self.items[k].queued).collect()
    }
    pub fn on_launched(&mut self, issue: u64, id: uuid::Uuid) {
        if let Some(it) = self.items.iter_mut().find(|i| i.queued.issue_number == issue) { it.session_id = Some(id); }
    }
    pub fn on_finished(&mut self, id: uuid::Uuid, outcome: Outcome) {
        let Some(k) = self.items.iter().position(|i| i.session_id == Some(id)) else { return }; // not ours
        match outcome {
            Outcome::Done => self.items[k].state = QueueItemState::Succeeded,
            Outcome::Failed | Outcome::Hollow => { self.items[k].state = QueueItemState::Failed; self.awaiting.push((k, outcome)); }
        }
    }
    pub fn worst_case(&self, spent_by: impl Fn(uuid::Uuid) -> f64, per_session: f64) -> f64 {
        self.items.iter().map(|i| match (i.state, i.session_id) {
            (QueueItemState::Succeeded | QueueItemState::Skipped, Some(id)) => spent_by(id),
            (QueueItemState::Skipped, None) => 0.0,
            _ => per_session,
        }).sum()
    }
}


// widgets/decision_card.rs (proposed): options with a price on the right; ratatui 0.29.
pub fn option_lines(o: &DecisionOption, on: bool, focused: bool, w: u16, t: &Theme) -> [Line<'static>; 2] {
    let cost: Vec<Span> = match o.cost {
        Cost::Free => vec![Span::styled("$0.00", Style::new().fg(t.accent_success))],
        Cost::Session { floor, cap } => vec![
            Span::styled(format!("est ≥ ${floor:.2}"), Style::new().fg(t.text_primary)),
            Span::styled(format!(" · stops at ${cap:.2}"), Style::new().fg(t.text_muted)),
        ],
    };
    let cw: usize = cost.iter().map(|s| s.width()).sum();
    let radio = if on { icons::get(IconId::DotFill) } else { icons::get(IconId::Circle) };
    let label = format!("{radio} {}", o.label);
    let fits = label.width() + 3 + cw <= w as usize;
    let mut head = vec![Span::raw(if on && focused { "▌" } else { " " }), Span::styled(label.clone(), Style::new().fg(t.text_primary))];
    let mut note = vec![Span::raw("   ")];
    if fits { head.push(Span::raw(" ".repeat(w as usize - label.width() - 1 - cw))); head.extend(cost); }
    else { note.extend(cost); note.push(Span::styled("  ·  ", Style::new().fg(t.text_muted))); }
    note.push(Span::styled(sanitize_for_terminal(&o.note), Style::new().fg(t.text_muted)));
    let head = Line::from(head);
    [if on && focused { head.style(focused_selection_style(t)) } else { head }, Line::from(note)]
}

02.23Diagnostics: gate output, CI error review, call log


Three read-the-failure screens: the output of failed local gates, the log of a failed CI check, and the list of an agent's tool and API calls. In v0.31.8 each is a separate popup or page with its own keys, and the gate page cannot show the failing tests at all. The redesign makes all three full-size views of screens that already exist. It groups failures by file with the first one open, shows time and cost per call, and puts a price and a review step in front of every action that spends money or pushes code.

Screen components




Failure digest (failureList): one parser output, two sources (local gate, CI step). Groups by file in output order; each item has a glyph (✗ test or error, ! warning), a name, an optional lint tag and :line:col. The first item is open; ⏎ opens or closes the item under the cursor. Long lines wrap; short lines keep the tool's own indentation (left:/right:, the clippy caret). When another panel has focus, the selected item is shown underlined in accent, with no selection bar, so only one place looks focused. g opens file:line in $EDITOR inside the session's worktree (proposed).




Cleaning external text. Every line from a gate, a CI log or a payload goes through one pipeline before it is drawn or sent to an agent: strip CSI/OSC sequences, then sanitize_for_terminal, then redact_secrets. CI line prefixes (job␉step␉timestamp) move to the panel title. The bottom border of each panel says what was done, so nobody wonders where the colours went.




Call row. TIME · KIND · WHAT · TOOK · TOKENS · COST · FLAG. Tool rows: tool name in magenta, argument, short result (41 passed, +17 −3), duration = ToolResult.timestamp − ToolUse.timestamp. Turn rows: first line of the reply, input + output tokens, cost from that message's CostUpdate. Kinds are words (tool turn think hook done error warn). Compact drops TOKENS.

Sessions from before the storage fix say that only 200 characters were kept, and that r gets the full output. An empty call log says how long the agent has been running.

// screens/mod.rs — one sanitizer for gate output, CI logs, session logs and payloads.
pub fn sanitize_for_terminal(s: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(s.len());
    let mut it = s.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = it.next() {
        if c == '\x1b' {
            match it.peek() {
                // CSI: ESC [ params… final byte in '@'..='~'
                Some('[') => { it.next(); for n in it.by_ref() { if ('@'..='~').contains(&n) { break; } } }
                // OSC: ESC ] … terminated by BEL or ESC \
                Some(']') => { it.next(); while let Some(n) = it.next() { if n == '\x07' { break; } if n == '\x1b' { it.next(); break; } } }
                _ => {}
            }
            continue;
        }
        out.push(if c.is_control() && c != '\n' { ' ' } else { c });
    }
    out
}


// widgets/failure_list.rs (proposed) — FAILURES BY FILE, first item open. Glyphs via icons::get in real code.
pub fn failure_lines<'a>(d: &'a Digest, sel: usize, open: &HashSet<usize>, focused: bool, theme: &Theme) -> Vec<Line<'a>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut idx = 0;
    for g in &d.groups {
        out.push(Line::from(vec![
            Span::styled(g.path.as_str(), Style::default().fg(theme.text_primary).add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
            Span::styled(format!("  {} failing", g.items.len()), Style::default().fg(theme.text_muted)),
        ]));
        for f in &g.items {
            let is_open = open.contains(&idx);
            let row = if idx == sel && focused { focused_selection_style(theme) } else { Style::default() };
            out.push(Line::from(vec![
                Span::raw(if is_open { " ▾ " } else { " ▸ " }),
                Span::styled("✗ ", Style::default().fg(theme.accent_error)),
                Span::styled(f.title.as_str(), Style::default().add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD)),
                Span::styled(format!("  :{}:{}", f.line, f.col), Style::default().fg(theme.text_muted)),
            ]).style(row));
            if is_open {
                out.extend(f.body.iter().map(|l| Line::from(format!("      {l}")))); // already sanitized in digest()
            }
            idx += 1;
        }
    }
    out
}

(2) Home's palette entry "Diagnostics" (network chart, release console) and these views share a name. Rename that entry to "Network & release"? (3) Are TokenUpdate/CostUpdate values per message or cumulative? manager.rs replaces session.cost_usd on each one ("the CLI emits cumulative totals"), while usage_events prices each message's own usage. 02.24Guards, release notes and small modals


Five small modes that guard or follow up on bigger actions: the bypass warning (⌃B), the pre-spawn budget gate, the code-health scan (TuiMode::Sanitize), the release notes behind Home's What's new, and the "Next iteration paths" list that follows a finished session. In v0.31.8 the two guards do not say what they guard: the bypass warning hides half of what it turns on, and the budget gate never fires in production. The redesign makes each guard state the exact effect, the money and the way back, and makes the other three normal crumb screens instead of pop-ups that steal focus.

TypedConfirm field: the same token rule as Settings' dangerBox, built on the canonical Input widget. It never closes on a typo; it marks the first wrong letter on the border and keeps ⏎ locked.




Spend gate, Warn (left) and Block (right). Same numbers as the real math: after = spent + max(cost_usd, per_session × 0.10); worst = spent + per-session cap. Warn is not "safe": here the worst case ($51.10) passes the cap, so the row says so. Block locks S; the way forward is b or waiting.




Code health writes: armed bar states for filing findings as issues (proposed), using the Settings armed-save chord (⌃S, then ⌃S or ⏎ within 3s). Below: the AI pass confirm, which spends money but writes nothing, so it is a dialog, not an armed bar.

// src/tui/screens/bypass_warning.rs — TypedConfirm on the canonical Input widget (widgets/input, ratatui 0.29)
pub struct BypassWarning { input: Input, effects: Effects }   // Input::single_line(InputConfig::new().max_len(16))

impl BypassWarning {
    pub fn handle_event(&mut self, event: &Event) -> BypassWarningOutcome {
        let Event::Key(key) = event else { return BypassWarningOutcome::Pending };
        match key.code {
            KeyCode::Esc => BypassWarningOutcome::Cancelled,
            KeyCode::Enter if self.input.text() == CONFIRM_PHRASE => BypassWarningOutcome::Confirmed,
            KeyCode::Enter => BypassWarningOutcome::Pending,              // locked: never cancels
            _ => { self.input.input(event.clone()); BypassWarningOutcome::Pending }
        }
    }
    /// First index where the typed text stops matching, for the border message.
    pub fn mismatch(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.input.text().chars().zip(CONFIRM_PHRASE.chars()).position(|(a, b)| a != b)
    }
}
// draw: widgets::input::render(&self.input, f, field_area, theme, true), then the mismatch on the bottom border.


// src/budget.rs (proposed) — one view model for the gate, the launch dialog and the Cost view
pub struct SpendView { pub spent: f64, pub next: f64, pub after: f64, pub worst: f64, pub cap: f64 }

impl SpendView {
    pub fn new(spent: f64, per_session: f64, floor: f64, session_cost: f64, cap: f64) -> Self {
        let next = sanitize_cost(session_cost).max(per_session * floor);
        Self { spent, next, after: spent + next, worst: spent + per_session, cap }
    }
    pub fn left(&self) -> f64 { (self.cap - self.spent).max(0.0) }
    pub fn blocks(&self) -> bool { self.after >= self.cap }        // same rule as check_pre_spawn
    pub fn worst_passes(&self) -> bool { self.worst >= self.cap }
}

04Components


Each component lists its variants, states and the poka-yoke rule it enforces. Names are proposals for a src/tui/ds/ module; several wrap things that already exist (keybinding_hints.rs, agent_badge.rs, budget_banner.rs, clipboard_toast.rs).



StatusBar ds::status_bar


State only, left to right by importance: brand · version · repo@branch · fleet counts · budget · quota · uptime. Right side: trust, update, mode. Segments drop from the right of the left group as width shrinks (uptime, then quota, then repo).




Poka-yoke: the mode chip is always visible and changes colour and word (NORMAL / INSERT / COMMAND), so typing into the wrong mode is visible at a glance. UNTRUSTED appears whenever the workspace trust gate is closed.

One entry per SessionStatus variant in src/session/types.rs. Statuses that need a human (NeedsReview, FailedGates, Errored) are bold too.

Variants: Inactive, Active, Overlay, Danger, Disabled (see Borders). Optional title badge (count) and right-aligned title hint (the key that opens its full screen).



ActionList ds::action_list






The old two-column menu, regrouped by intent (proximity: related actions sit together). Letters are unchanged, so existing muscle memory still works.


  • Selected: reverse video plus ▌ marker, so it survives NO_COLOR.
    • 

  • Badge: right-aligned count (pool sessions, adoptable sessions).
    • 

  • Disabled: dimmed with ⊘. Selecting it shows the reason and the fix ("no milestones yet · m creates one"). It never silently does nothing.
    • 

  • Removed: Quit. Leaving the app is a global command, not a destination.



AttentionQueue ds::attention_queue new


This is the main productivity change. It is built from signals the app already computes: FailedGates/Errored, NeedsReview, NeedsPr, CiFix/ConflictFix, budget_banner and quota_refresh. Rank: error > waiting on human > ready to ship > resource notice; ties go to the oldest item.




Poka-yoke: one primary action per row, always on ⏎. An earlier draft used per-row letters (g gates, p open PR), but p already means PRD on Home. The keymap test in Implementation would have caught that collision. The empty state teaches the next step instead of showing a blank box. When the queue is non-empty, the terminal title becomes (3) maestro, so you see it from another tab.



FleetTable ds::fleet_table


Wide: 7 columns. Compact: AGENT · ISSUE · STATUS · CTX · COST. Context gauge turns warn at 80%. In v0.31.8 context_overflow.rs nudges a commit at 50% and auto-forks at 70% when the AutoFork flag is on; the gauge marks whichever threshold is active.





Gauge ds::gauge


Thresholds are shared by budget, quota windows and context: <60% accent · ≥60% warn (routing shifts) · ≥80% error · ≥100% error bold with a block reason. The percentage label is always printed next to the bar.





Charts & Canvas ratatui::widgets::{Sparkline, BarChart, canvas::Canvas}


Each chart answers one question and states its unit and window. Canvas with Marker::Braille gives 2×4 sub-cell resolution for throughput; horizontal bars replace the unlabeled vertical mix chart.





ActivityLog ds::activity_log


Columns: time · level · source · message. Level filter in the title (all · warn · err), / to search. Wraps activity_log.rs and log_viewer.rs.





Toast ds::toast


Rounded overlay, bottom-right, at most 2 stacked. Success toasts for reversible actions carry ⌃Z undo and a visible countdown. Error toasts carry the fix, not just the failure.





Confirm dialogs ds::confirm::{HoldToConfirm, TypedConfirm}


Double border, error colour, backdrop dimmed. The default action is always the safe one, and ⏎ never confirms a destructive dialog. Each dialog states what is kept, not only what is lost.




Terminals only report key release when the kitty keyboard protocol is on (KeyboardEnhancementFlags::REPORT_EVENT_TYPES). Where supports_keyboard_enhancement() is false, HoldToConfirm falls back to press-twice-within-2s, with the same progress bar.



CommandPalette ds::palette new


⌃K from anywhere. Fuzzy search over every keymap action, showing its key, so the palette also teaches shortcuts. Destructive entries are red and still go through their confirm. Opening it switches the mode chip to INSERT.





Kit v2 armedBar subTabs filterChips kpiTile mdBlock treePrefix dialog toast promoted

armedBar: one component for every external or irreversible write. States: blocked → ready → armed (⏎ again within 3s) → working → done | failed.




subTabs sub-views · filterChips · sectionLabel · kpiTile (value, delta, sparkline, loading/error) · mdBlock (headings, checklists, `code`, #refs, TODO chips) · treePrefix · readyStrip.




dialog (overlay / danger, dims the backdrop) and toast (bottom-right, ⌃Z undo countdown).

Breakpoints and the Home layout


use ratatui::layout::{Constraint, Layout, Rect};

pub const MIN_SIZE: (u16, u16) = (80, 24);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Breakpoint { Compact, Regular, Wide }

impl Breakpoint {
    /// `None` means "draw the SizeGuard instead".
    pub fn from_area(area: Rect) -> Option<Self> {
        if area.width < MIN_SIZE.0 || area.height < MIN_SIZE.1 {
            return None;
        }
        Some(match area.width {
            0..=99 => Self::Compact,
            100..=149 => Self::Regular,
            _ => Self::Wide,
        })
    }
}

pub fn draw_home(f: &mut Frame, app: &App, theme: &Theme) {
    let Some(bp) = Breakpoint::from_area(f.area()) else {
        return size_guard::render(f, f.area(), theme);
    };
    let banner_h = u16::from(app.budget_banner().is_some());
    let [status, tabs, banner, body, footer] = Layout::vertical([
        Constraint::Length(1),
        Constraint::Length(1),
        Constraint::Length(banner_h),
        Constraint::Fill(1),
        Constraint::Length(1),
    ])
    .areas(f.area());

    let attn_h = app.attention().len().max(3) as u16 + 2;
    let fleet_h = app.sessions().len().max(2) as u16 + 3;
    match bp {
        Breakpoint::Wide => {
            let [left, center, right] = Layout::horizontal([
                Constraint::Length(26), Constraint::Fill(1), Constraint::Length(44),
            ]).areas(body);
            let [needs, fleet, log] = Layout::vertical([
                Constraint::Length(attn_h), Constraint::Length(fleet_h), Constraint::Fill(1),
            ]).areas(center);
            // … render each region with ds:: widgets
        }
        Breakpoint::Regular => { /* drop the insight column, quota becomes a strip */ }
        Breakpoint::Compact => { /* single column */ }
    }
}



Panel: one focus signal


use ratatui::{style::{Modifier, Style}, text::Line, widgets::{Block, BorderType}};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Focus { Inactive, Active, Overlay, Danger, Disabled }

pub fn panel<'a>(title: &'a str, focus: Focus, t: &Theme) -> Block<'a> {
    let (kind, color) = match focus {
        Focus::Inactive => (BorderType::Plain, t.border_inactive),
        Focus::Active   => (BorderType::Thick, t.border_active),
        Focus::Overlay  => (BorderType::Rounded, t.accent_info),
        Focus::Danger   => (BorderType::Double, t.accent_error),
        Focus::Disabled => (BorderType::Plain, t.text_muted),
    };
    let mut border = Style::new().fg(color);
    let mut title_style = Style::new().add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD).fg(match focus {
        Focus::Inactive => t.text_primary,
        _ => color,
    });
    if focus == Focus::Disabled {
        border = border.add_modifier(Modifier::DIM);
        title_style = title_style.add_modifier(Modifier::DIM);
    }
    Block::bordered()
        .border_type(kind)
        .border_style(border)
        .title(Line::styled(format!(" {title} "), title_style))
}



StatusChip: glyph + label + colour


pub fn status_chip(status: SessionStatus, t: &Theme) -> Line<'static> {
    let (glyph, label) = status_glyph(status); // icons registry; ASCII when MAESTRO_ASCII_ICONS=1
    let mut style = Style::new().fg(t.status_color(status));
    if matches!(status, SessionStatus::NeedsReview | SessionStatus::FailedGates | SessionStatus::Errored) {
        style = style.add_modifier(Modifier::BOLD);
    }
    Line::from(vec![Span::styled(glyph, style), Span::raw(" "), Span::styled(label, style)])
}



HoldToConfirm


use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyEventKind};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

const DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum HoldMode { KeyRelease, DoubleTap } // KeyRelease needs REPORT_EVENT_TYPES

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
pub enum Hold { Idle, Armed, Progress(f32), Confirmed, Cancelled }

pub struct HoldToConfirm {
    mode: HoldMode,
    hold: Duration,            // 500ms
    started: Option<Instant>,  // KeyRelease mode
    armed: Option<Instant>,    // DoubleTap mode
}

impl HoldToConfirm {
    pub fn on_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent, now: Instant) -> Hold {
        if key.code == KeyCode::Esc {
            self.reset();
            return Hold::Cancelled;
        }
        if key.code != KeyCode::Char('Q') {
            return Hold::Idle; // Enter, lowercase q, everything else: inert
        }
        match (self.mode, key.kind) {
            (HoldMode::KeyRelease, KeyEventKind::Release) => { self.reset(); Hold::Idle }
            (HoldMode::KeyRelease, _) => {
                let start = *self.started.get_or_insert(now);
                self.progress(now.duration_since(start))
            }
            (HoldMode::DoubleTap, KeyEventKind::Press) => match self.armed.replace(now) {
                Some(t) if now.duration_since(t) <= DOUBLE_TAP_WINDOW => { self.reset(); Hold::Confirmed }
                _ => Hold::Armed,
            },
            _ => Hold::Idle,
        }
    }

    /// Called on the app tick so the bar fills between OS key-repeat events.
    pub fn tick(&self, now: Instant) -> Hold {
        match self.started {
            Some(start) => self.progress(now.duration_since(start)),
            None => Hold::Idle,
        }
    }

    fn progress(&self, held: Duration) -> Hold {
        if held >= self.hold { Hold::Confirmed }
        else { Hold::Progress(held.as_secs_f32() / self.hold.as_secs_f32()) }
    }

    fn reset(&mut self) { self.started = None; self.armed = None; }
}



Keymap registry: collisions fail the build


#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct Chord { pub code: KeyCode, pub mods: KeyModifiers }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Danger { Safe, Reversible, Destructive }

pub struct Binding { pub chord: Chord, pub scope: Scope, pub action: Action, pub danger: Danger }

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::collections::HashMap;

    #[test]
    fn keymap_is_poka_yoke_clean() {
        for scope in Scope::ALL {
            let mut seen: HashMap<Chord, Action> = HashMap::new();
            // a scope sees its own bindings plus every enclosing scope's
            for b in KEYMAP.iter().filter(|b| b.scope.encloses(*scope)) {
                if let Some(prev) = seen.insert(b.chord, b.action) {
                    panic!("{scope:?}: {:?} bound to both {prev:?} and {:?}", b.chord, b.action);
                }
                if b.danger == Danger::Destructive {
                    assert!(b.chord.is_uppercase_or_ctrl(), "{:?} is destructive on a bare lowercase key", b.action);
                    assert!(b.action.requires_confirm(), "{:?} is destructive without a confirm step", b.action);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
